jobs.title: Field Service Engineer Protection
jobs.description:
Job Description Summary

As a Protection Commissioning Engineer at GE Vernova, you will serve as a technical authority responsible for the commissioning, optimization, and lifecycle support of advanced protection systems across the India and SSA regions. You will act as the primary interface between GE Vernova and our customers, ensuring high-quality, safe, and efficient project delivery while leading the resolution of complex protection and control challenges at site.

Job Description

Technical Domain Expertise

The ideal candidate must demonstrate expert-level, hands-on experience with industry-standard protection platforms across the following domains:

• Generator Protection: Configuration and testing of complex schemes for large-scale generation assets (GE Vernova G60, MiCOM P343, Siemens 7UMx, ABB REG670).
• Busbar Protection (BBP): Proficiency in both high and low-impedance schemes. Mandatory: Deep conceptual and testing knowledge of P741/P743 (Distributed) and P746 (Centralized) architectures.
• Line Protection: Advanced application of distance (MHO/Quadrilateral) and differential protection, including tele-protection schemes (POTT, PUTT, Blocking). Experience with GE Vernova P54x/L90, Siemens 7SL, ABB RED670, and SEL 411L.
• Transformer Protection: Implementation and testing of differential (87T), REF, and overcurrent/earth fault logic (GEV P64x/T60, Siemens 7UTx, ABB RET670, SEL 487E).
• Backup Protection: Extensive experience with auxiliary Overcurrent (OC) and Earth Fault (EF) protection across diverse relay makes.

Core Responsibilities

• Commissioning Excellence: Possesses in-depth knowledge of substation protection systems, relay technologies, and protection philosophies across Generator, Transformer, Transmission Line, Busbar, and Backup protection schemes and communication devices, ensuring robust IED integration with SCADA systems.
• Technical Troubleshooting: Conduct root-cause analysis and onsite diagnostics, strictly adhering to GE Vernova safety protocols.
• System Optimization: Execute relay setting reviews, tripping analyses, and coordination studies to ensure grid stability, selectivity, and sensitivity.
• Customer & Technical Leadership: Serve as the primary technical point of contact for clients; mentor junior engineers and provide cross-functional leadership.
• Operational Proficiency: Expert use of secondary injection test kits (Omicron, ISA, Doble, Megger) and ability to interpret complex schematic drawings.
• Continuous Improvement: Manage "Record of Experience" (ROE) documentation to drive internal learning and prevent recurring technical issues.

Qualifications

• Education: Bachelor’s degree in electrical or Electronics & Communication Engineering.
• Experience: Minimum 4+ years of professional experience in substation protection and commissioning.
• Language: High proficiency in English (Read/Write/Speak) and Hindi; additional regional languages are an asset.
• Mobility: Willingness to undertake extensive, long-duration travel across India and the SSA region.

Key Competencies

• Technical Expertise: Good knowledge of substation protection systems, relay technologies, and protection philosophies across various numerical relays.
• Communication: Demonstrates excellent verbal and written communication skills, enabling effective interaction with customers, project stakeholders, and cross-functional teams.
• Leadership & Mentorship: Exhibits strong supervisory and team coordination abilities, with a proven track record of guiding and mentoring junior engineers to achieve project milestones.
• Problem-Solving: Proficient in performing root-cause analysis, identifying technical bottlenecks, and implementing effective, sustainable solutions in high-pressure field environments.
• Quality & Safety Focus: Maintains an unwavering commitment to high standards of quality, operational compliance, and strict adherence to safety protocols

Additional Information

Relocation Assistance Provided: Yes

jobs.title: Billing Specialist
jobs.description:
The Billing Specialist processes the daily deposit for payment of attorney invoices and is assigned to specific ebilling systems and clients to ensure the attorney invoices are properly uploaded for payment approval. The Billing Specialist also performs a variety of other accounting duties, including collections according to our established policies and procedures.

Maintains contact with attorneys, staff, vendors, clients regarding invoice status with the E-Billing systems and demonstrates confidentiality of client and firm matters.

Essential Job Functions:

• Submit invoices through various e-billing platforms.

• Performs the daily deposits.

• Applies paper checks, ACH/EFT payments, and credit card payments to the appropriate case and invoice as directed by clients daily.

• Processes refunds for overpayments on invoices when needed, saving all documentation to the specific case in our system.
• Research and applies prepaids in our system to the appropriate case and maintains the itemized prepaid spreadsheet daily.
• Research the outstanding WIP for all clients in our system- processing deletions, updating and maintaining the billing entries in our system and the spreadsheet on a weekly basis for accuracy.

• Adding ACH clients upon request and maintenance of the ACH spreadsheet in our system for full accuracy.

• Maintenance of the spreadsheet for paper billed clients upon request when changes occur.

• Possible future handling of specific clients within assigned bill review systems.

• Communicates with the electronic bill review systems, attorneys, staff and adjusters for each client when needed, to ensure the invoices are successfully uploaded and approved.

• Works with clients to ensure budgets and matter are added to the electronic bill review system which resolves any possible rejection issues that surface during the uploading process.

• Reviews and verifies accuracy of billing and supporting documentation as required.

• Is familiar with and applies Firm billing guidelines with each of their assigned clients within the bill review systems.

• Maintains collections of specific electronically billed clients.

• Saves collection efforts/emails to cases in our system.

• Processes write-offs following Firm policy.

• Creates and distributes accounts receivable reports when requested.

• Ensure strict confidentiality at all times.

• Assists with special projects as needed.

• Other duties as assigned.

• High school diploma or GED (or equivalent) required; associate or bachelor's degree in accounting preferred.

• Experience with ebilling platforms required, e.g., TyMetrix, LegalX, etc.
• 1-2+ years e-billing and accounts receivable experience in a law firm.
• Perfect Law Legal software experience preferred.
• Proficiency with Microsoft Office.

• Ability to handle a high volume of invoices each month.

• Ability to effectively communicate with attorneys, staff, and clients.

• Ability to organize workflows and use time efficiently via multitasking and prioritization.

• Strong attention to detail in a fast-paced, ever-changing work environment and successfully adapt to changing priorities and work demands.

• Ability to anticipate work needs and follow through with minimum direction, follow up on own initiative

• Firm and Client Confidentiality required.

Benefits include: Medical, Dental, Vision, Group Term Life Insurance, Voluntary Term Life Insurance, Critical Illness, Accident, HSA, FSA, pre-tax Transit and pre-tax Parking. 401(k)/Roth retirement plan with company match. Generous time off policy.

All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

jobs.title: People Operations Specialist (Contract SF/Remote, A1313)
jobs.description:

You will support projects tied to People team tooling, employee data, and compliance, working closely with People Partners, Payroll, Legal, IT, and Internal Tools. You will work across Workday, Greenhouse, and Checkr, and your attention to detail and commitment to process improvement will keep employee data accurate and employee experiences smooth.

Onboarding - Own day-to-day onboarding execution for large new hire cohorts: coordinate start dates, communicate with incoming employees, and keep the onboarding experience organized - Work alongside existing team members to handle volume and cover for each other as weekly onboarding is adopted

Contingent Worker Onboarding - Collect required information, initiate background checks, send welcome communications, and coordinate start dates with managers

Conversions and Status Changes - Process full-time to part-time conversions, contractor modifications, and vendor communications

HRIS Administration - Maintain employee records in Workday, process status changes and updates, and ensure data accuracy across systems - Partner with People Partners and managers when employee records need to be updated or corrected

People Tickets and Documentation - Triage and respond to internal employee questions and requests, and maintain the people tickets queue - Build and maintain onboarding guides, process playbooks, and FAQs so employees and the team can find what they need

Qualifications -

• 5+ years of experience in People Operations, HR operations, or HRIS administration
• Experience at other tech companies, ideally fast-growing organizations
• Workday (HRIS) experience strongly recommended; Greenhouse or similar HR systems experience a plus
• Organized and detail-oriented, with excellent professional judgment when managing time-sensitive processes related to compensation, performance, and compliance
• Careful handling of employee data, with a firm commitment to accuracy and privacy
• Reliable and responsive when fielding urgent questions from employees and People team partners
• Excellent communication skills for coordinating with cross-functional partners
• Able to manage multiple deadlines and prioritize effectively as priorities shift
• Customer service oriented, treating internal teams as clients, with a flexible and creative approach to problem-solving
• Comfortable working as part of a small team, collaborating daily on onboarding and tickets and supporting each other during busy periods

Additional Information

• Contract, approximately 6 months
• Full time, 40 hours per week.

All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

jobs.title: Tissue Recovery Specialist - (Funeral Services professionals - apply here)
jobs.description:
Looking for meaningful work, great benefits and a place to belong? We will train the right applicant… so join us, we'd love to have you on our team!

You have the opportunity to advance your healthcare career at New England Donor Services by joining a dynamic, professional team whose mission is to save and heal lives through tissue donation.

As a Tissue Recovery Specialist, you will become a member of a professional surgical team where you will have hands on paid training to learn to aseptically remove bones, skin, veins, corneas, heart-for-valves and additional tissues from deceased donors while developing your technical skills in ways you never imagined possible.

Tissue donations are pivotal in helping children who require heart valve transplants lead full and healthy lives, breast cancer survivors in need of mastectomy surgeries feel whole again, restoring sight to those who suffer from corneal blindness, and so many others.

About you:

Your colleagues should describe you as a positive team player, self-motivated, detail-oriented, and mission-driven. You take great pride in your work and are motivated by the thought of being able to touch countless lives as a direct result of your work and through our mission. Candidates with Funeral Services, EMT, Paramedic, ER Tech, OR Tech or Surgical Tech backgrounds with medical terminology and anatomy background strongly encouraged to apply!

Schedule:

As a full-time employee, you will be scheduled for 3 12-hour shifts per week. The schedule is comprised of 2 shifts that run for 12 weeks at a time.

Days 7:00 am-7:00 pm

Evenings 12:00 pm-12:00 am

You will have every other weekend off, and the standard 1.5 overtime calculation will apply for hours worked beyond 40 hours in a given workweek. Additional mandatory training and meetings required.

Travel:

This position is based in Waltham, MA. However, it is likely you will travel throughout New England in NEDS vehicles. Must be comfortable with long periods of driving and possible travel in a small aircraft. Must live within a reasonable driving distance from the Waltham location.

Candidates will be required to travel by personal vehicle to meet the duties and responsibilities of this position. Must maintain the requirements of an “eligible driver” including being at least 21 years old, maintaining an acceptable Motor Vehicle Record (MVR) and required minimum personal automobile insurance per NEDS automobile policy.

Please note: We are currently interviewing for New Hire Orientation class for Decemeber 2026

The ideal candidate is self-motivated, disciplined, detail-oriented, independent, adaptable, team-oriented and possesses the stamina required to succeed in this intense and rewarding clinical setting.

• Associates degree or minimum 2 years professional experience as an EMT, Paramedic, ER Tech, OR Tech - hands on healthcare experience is a must!
• Demonstrated excellent verbal and written communication skills
• Must have a valid driver’s license and a safe driving record
• Must be able to lift up to 75 lbs.
• Must be able to stand for extended periods of time
• Annual influenza vaccination is required for employees who work in a clinical or healthcare environment outside of NEDS facilities.

Additional Requirements:

• Must be able to thrive in a complex, fast-paced environment
• Ability to apply critical thinking skills by multi-tasking and applying Standard Operating Procedures during day-to-day work functions
• Must be able to manage multiple systems and computer applications
• Must have an intermediate understanding of medical terminology
• Ability to adapt to variable working conditions

When you join New England Donor Services you can expect competitive salaries and a great benefit package. Benefits include a generous paid time off program, BCBS Health and Dental Insurance, Healthcare Reimbursement Account, 2x Annual Salary Life Insurance, Pet Insurance, Flexible Spending Account (FSA), Short-Term and Long-Term Disability Coverage, 403(b) Retirement Contribution, Tuition Reimbursement, Employee Assistance Program and Discounts through Working Advantage.

New England Donor Services is an equal opportunity employer and welcomes candidates from all backgrounds to apply to meet the needs of the communities we serve.

jobs.title: Finance Data Product Analyst — FP&A
jobs.description:
Primary Function of Position

The Finance Data Product Analyst will serve as the dedicated FP&A analytics support resource, owning the requirements-to-handoff lifecycle across core FP&A domains. This role fills a current gap where FP&A requirements gathering, stakeholder coordination, and AI-to-engineering handoff are absorbed across leads without dedicated capacity. The analyst will ensure faster turnaround, stronger domain ownership across GLTD, Revenue, CapEx, and HC portfolios, and less rework in downstream deliverables.

Roles and Responsibilities

Serve as the dedicated FP&A analyst for requirements intake — gather, clarify, document, and prioritize business requirements from Finance stakeholders across GLTD, Revenue, CapEx, and HC portfolios.

Translate business requirements into structured technical specifications and data model requirements for handoff to the onsite senior analyst and engineering team.

Own the requirements-to-engineering handoff process — ensure specifications are complete, unambiguous, and validated before passing to development, reducing rework cycles.

Perform data validation, reconciliation, and UAT support — verify that delivered models and reports match business intent and source data.

Debug and trace data through existing EDW models to answer stakeholder questions, identify discrepancies, and document root causes for engineering resolution.

Coordinate between onsite and offshore teams — manage requirements backlogs, track delivery status, flag gaps or conflicts, and ensure timely handoff at each stage.

Maintain documentation: business requirements documents, data dictionaries, test cases, and process guides.

Support AI-augmented analytics adoption by articulating business needs that could benefit from AI/ML capabilities and translating them into actionable requirements.

Qualifications

Required Skills and Experience

4 years of experience in BI analysis, data product analysis, or finance analytics support roles.

Strong understanding of FP&A concepts — general ledger, revenue recognition, CapEx planning, headcount reporting, cost center hierarchies.

SQL proficiency for data investigation — ability to query, trace, and validate data across EDW layers (not expected to build pipelines).

Experience with requirements gathering, documentation, and business-to-technical translation.

Familiarity with Snowflake or similar cloud data platforms from an analyst/consumer perspective.

Experience with Tableau or similar BI tools for report validation and basic analysis.

Strong written and verbal communication — ability to write clear specs and coordinate across time zones with onsite teams.

Detail-oriented with a structured approach to tracking deliverables and handoff checklists.

Preferred Qualifications

SAP Finance or ERP data familiarity (GL, AP, AR, cost center structures).

Exposure to AI/ML concepts — enough to recognize where AI-assisted analytics could add value to FP&A workflows.

Experience working in offshore delivery models with structured SDLC or agile processes.

Knowledge of data governance and data quality practices.

Required Education and Training

Bachelor's degree in finance, computer science, mathematics, information systems, or business.

he Transportation Specialist is responsible for executing standard operational workflows and ensuring the smooth operation of our logistical activities. The Specialist ensures performance and lowest-cost transportation by analyzing company and customer needs, researching transportation methods, and resolving operational bottlenecks.

• Proactively identify, address, and resolve operational issues that may impact customer satisfaction, working on solutions to improve the overall customer experience.

• Drive carrier and service provider performance for the Hub and Spoke locations.

• Serve as a primary point of contact for internal departments, external vendors, and customers regarding logistics-related inquiries and issue resolution.
• Act as a liaison between the warehouse vendor and carrier, ensuring standard operating procedures (SOPs) are followed.
• Support domestic and international shipments, ensuring partner carriers meet requirements for critical shipments.
• Monitor inbound and outbound deliveries, proactively resolving bottlenecks in the shipping and receiving processes.

• Bachelor's degree or equivalent working experience.
• 2–4 years of experience in supply chain, logistics, and/or transportation.
• Solid experience with logistics software and systems, such as ERP systems, transportation management systems (TMS), and warehouse management systems (WMS).

• Effective communication, negotiation, and issue-resolution skills.

jobs.title: Maintenance Technician I
jobs.description:
Position Purpose:

The Maintenance Technician I, inspects, maintains, repairs and installs mechanical, electromechanical, pneumatic and/or hydraulic equipment at plant and/or pump stations. Operate Centrifuge, Dump Truck, Sewer Cleaning Jet/Vac Equipment. Perform Maintenance and Operational Task with minimum oversight.

Primary Duties/Responsibilities:

• Operate the centrifuge and drive a 10 ton dump truck and sewer jet truck as well as lift station inspection and repairs.
• Performs routine and preventative maintenance, lubrication and minor adjustments on machines and related equipment which may include pumps, engines, centrifuges, generators, valves, gates, mixers, conveyors, blowers, dryers, chemical feed and odor control, disinfection equipment, vacuum filters and belt presses. Promptly reports any operational problems with machines or equipment to Lead or Supervisor.
• Learns to inspect and becomes proficient at mechanical troubleshooting to determine repairs needed. Dismantles equipment to gain access to and repairs defective parts using hand tools, power tools and precision measuring and testing devices. Re-assembles and tests equipment ensuring safe and efficient operating conditions are restored. Learns to troubleshoot hydraulic, pneumatic and electronic equipment and instrumentation.
• Performs facility maintenance and repair and may replace or install light bulbs, fluorescent tubes, damaged glass, windows, doors, partitions, ceiling or floor tiles, door locks, carpet, and/or paint.
• May perform manual labor including cleaning equipment, facilities and grounds as required and properly dispose of waste according to safety and environmental policies. Operates vehicles for plant operational purposes.
• Cover on call rotation for both the Water and Wastewater plants.
• Learn to estimate time and material costs for various projects. May assist in other areas of the plant as directed.

Work Environment:

• Spends 100% of the time in the operations environment.
• Typically spends 25 – 35% of time exposed to outdoor and sometimes inclement weather.
• Company service vehicles are used as required.
• Travels 1 – 2 times per year for company provided training.
• Serves rotational 24 hour emergency on-call.
• Possible Work Hazards: May be exposed to possible operations hazards including fumes, dust, toxic and caustic chemicals, noise, rotating machinery, high pressure and hot and cold temperatures, slippery surfaces, water and electrical hazards.

Education/Experience/Background:

• High School Diploma or GED with the ability to read, write and comprehend English (operational, process, safety and quality instructions) and be able to carry out verbal and written instructions.
• Six months to two years of experience in a related position with ability to comprehend specifications, blueprints and manuals.
• Experience using power, pneumatic, hydraulic, and hand tools and shop tools such as drill press, band saw, bench grinder, and torque wrench preferred.
• Experience using material handling equipment, pressure gauges and precision measuring instruments.

Knowledge/Skills/Abilities:

• Ability to perform basic mathematical calculations.
• Some vocational training and mechanical aptitude preferred, with the ability to read, interpret and record data from meters, gauges, scales, panels, computer consoles and other equipment.
• Must have ability to operate Computer Maintenance Management System (software).
• Must consistently demonstrate the ability to learn and independently perform assigned duties and meet or exceed production and quality goals.
• Must demonstrate ability to work in a team environment and willingness to assume additional or new responsibilities readily

Required Certification/Licenses/Training:

• Must possess, or be able to obtain within three months, a commercial license class B with air brakes and tanker endorsement.
• Minimum water / wastewater license as required by regulatory agency at site - preferred
• Ability to be certified to perform public drinking water analysis within six months - required.
• Must possess a valid driver’s license and a safe driving record.
• Employee Orientation, Departmental Operating Procedures, Safety, Confined Space training, OSHA and Quality Training.
• HAZWOPER (Hazardous Waste Operations and Emergency Response) Level I and II First Responder Certification if required by site.
• Must become proficient in the care and use of all site specific, facility required PPE (Personal Protection Equipment), including respirators, gas detectors, confined space equipment, etc.)
• Forklift Certification if required by site.
• Training in operation of mechanical drives, hydraulic pumps and valves, pneumatics, electronics and control systems.
• Obtain or maintain HVAC, Electrician, Plumber’s or other trade License if assigned to that area.
• Note: Tech will not perform duties unless properly licensed.
• Training in the use of energy management systems as needed.
• Works toward increasing skills in additional functional areas or in obtaining advanced skills / maintenance certifications.

Physical Requirements:

• Amount of time spent – Standing 25%, Walking 75% for as many as five miles per shift.
• Requires close visual and hearing observation to detect non-conformance and machine malfunction.
• Constantly uses hands to finger, handle or feel and frequently reaches with hands and arms.
• Works in various positions; works on ladders, catwalks, and supports at heights of 50 feet above the ground; and works with hands extended above and below head and body up to 40 minutes using hand tools weighing up to 15 pounds.
• Must be able to lift and carry 50 pounds (occasionally 60 pounds) distances of 10 feet.
• Occasional stooping, bending or kneeling and entering confined spaces.

AECOM is actively seeking a motivated, hands-on Construction Materials & Quality Control Technician / Field Runner to support major transportation infrastructure projects throughout Utah. This position plays a critical role in ensuring the quality, safety, and long-term performance of roadway and transportation improvements for the Utah Department of Transportation (UDOT) and other public agency clients.

If you enjoy being outdoors, working on active construction projects, solving problems in the field, and contributing to projects that improve how communities move and connect, this opportunity offers a rewarding career path with exposure to some of Utah's most impactful infrastructure investments.

In this role, you will support construction teams by performing materials testing, documenting quality control activities, coordinating field operations, and assisting project staff with the collection and delivery of samples, reports, and project-related materials. You will work closely with inspectors, contractors, laboratory personnel, and project managers to help ensure construction activities meet project specifications, quality standards, and regulatory requirements.

• Collect, transport, and track material samples between project sites and testing laboratories.
• Conduct daily field observations and inspections to verify compliance with project plans, specifications, and quality requirements.
• Maintain accurate testing records, inspection reports, and project documentation.
• Support quality assurance and quality control efforts on active construction projects.
• Coordinate with contractors, inspectors, laboratory staff, and project teams regarding testing schedules and project needs.
• Assist with monitoring construction activities and documenting project progress.
• Participate in punch list activities, testing, and project closeout efforts.
• Track quality-related issues and communicate findings to project stakeholders.
• Utilize experience and judgment to prioritize assignments and meet project deadlines.
• Provide on-the-job guidance and training to less experienced team members as needed.
• Safely operate company vehicles and travel to project sites throughout the region.

• High School diploma or equivalent plus 2 years of related experience, or demonstrated equivalency through a combination of education and experience.
• A valid driver's license is required, along with the ability to pass a Motor Vehicle Records (MVR) check in accordance with company policy
• Ability to lift and carry at least 50 pounds on a consistent basis.
• Ability to work outdoors in varying weather conditions and active construction environments.

• SRDTT Concrete Testing Certification.
• Prior UDOT construction inspection or materials testing experience.
• Previous experience working with a municipal, county, or state transportation agency.

jobs.title: Wireless Field Engineer
jobs.description:
AECOM is seeking a Radio Frequency (RF) Field Engineer to be based in our Washington, DC office.  The RF Field Engineer will be responsible for data collection of various networks using RF measurement equipment and software tools.  The candidate will be responsible for testing and troubleshooting system components including performing cable testing using cable analyzer equipment, Passive Intermodulation (PIM) testing using PIM test equipment, and analyzing collected data to provide recommendations. The candidate will perform physical inspection systems including active and passive components such as radio transmitters, bi-directional amplifiers, splitters, connectors, coaxial cable, fiber cable, antennas, etc.

Essential Job Functions:

• Perform RF data collection using a scanner and spectrum analyzer
• Perform Insertion Loss (IL) test, according to the RF Cable Acceptance Test Procedure
• Perform Distance to Fault (DTF) test, according to the RF Cable Acceptance Test Procedure
• Perform PIM test, according to PIM Test Procedure
• Test fiber cable using fiber test equipment according to the Fiber Test Procedure
• Analyze test data and provide recommendations to resolve issues
• Commission small to medium-scale DAS networks
• Troubleshoot and repair RF systems in consultation with the Engineering team
• Inspect and analyze systems for any physical issues
• Perform site walks at various client locations to support system design
• Assist the Engineering Team with the analysis of existing systems and design for new systems
• Design small to medium-scale systems using software such as iBwave
• Will assist the radio design team in testing, analyzing, and servicing LMR and mobile phone networks

Minimum Requirements:

• High School plus eight years of related experience or demonstrated equivalency of experience and/or education
• Valid US Driver’s license
• U.S. Citizenship
• Ability to climb fixed ladders (≥ 24 ft) and work in dusty spaces

Preferred Qualifications:

• 3 years experience in the installation, commissioning, and maintenance of mobile phone and public safety Distributed Antenna Systems (or “DAS”) networks
• Experience in the installation and maintenance of Land Mobile Radio (LMR) systems preferred
• 2 years experience in RF cable, fiber, and communication systems
• Experience in coaxial and fiber cable testing
• Experience in using data collection tools and software
• Professional experience utilizing the following industry standard tools: • Data collection tools such as PCTel scanner, JDSU, or TEMs • Cable Testers such as Anritsu S332E or equivalent • Fiber Testers such as Fluke, OTR • PIM Testers such as Kaelus or Anritsu • Signal Generators
• Detail and safety-oriented

• Experience working with APIs to interact with gambling or financial platforms, and with backend development using frameworks like Django or Express.js.

Familiarity with the requirements of these licenses, including player protection, taxation, and financial reporting.

• Cryptocurrency Regulations: Expertise in the evolving legal landscape surrounding cryptocurrencies, including AML (Anti-Money Laundering) and KYC (Know Your Customer) rules. Understanding how crypto is regulated in various jurisdictions is essential, particularly for gambling transactions.

jobs.title: Geospatial Analyst
jobs.description:
AECOM is seeking a Geospatial Analyst to join our U.S. West Planning + Urbanism team. This role will support the Planning + Urbanism team in developing, analyzing, and managing spatial data and translating it into project deliverables that clearly visualize the analysis and key findings in maps, charts, tables, and infographics as well as writing. Applicants are expected to have experience with long-range planning and be able to interpret zoning or development regulations. No two projects our team works on are alike so creativity and critical thinking skills are a must.  This position will be located in hybrid capacity out of our Chicago or Dallas office

Job Description

The Geospatial Analyst will apply GIS technologies and spatial analysis techniques to support planning, design, environmental, infrastructure, and operational projects. The successful candidate will work collaboratively with project managers, planners, designers and technical specialists to transform complex geospatial information into actionable insights.

Responsibilities include but are not limited to:

• Perform geospatial analysis, data development, mapping, and visualization in support of multidisciplinary projects.
• Create, maintain, and manage vector, raster, imagery, and tabular geospatial datasets.
• Develop high-quality maps, figures, dashboards, and other geospatial products for technical reports, presentations, and client deliverables.
• Conduct spatial queries, geoprocessing, suitability analysis, proximity analysis, network analysis, and other advanced GIS workflows.
• Support collection, quality assurance, validation, and documentation of spatial data.
• Integrate data from multiple internal and external sources, including GPS/GNSS, CAD, remote sensing, imagery, and enterprise databases.
• Use ArcGIS Pro, ArcGIS Online, and related Esri applications to develop and maintain geospatial solutions.
• Assist with web GIS applications, dashboards, story maps, field data collection solutions, and enterprise GIS environments.
• Automate repeatable GIS processes using Python, ModelBuilder, SQL, or related tools where appropriate.
• Maintain metadata, data standards, naming conventions, and quality-control procedures.
• Coordinate with technical teams to understand project requirements and recommend appropriate geospatial methodologies.

jobs.description:
AECOM is seeking an experienced Secure Facilities Technical Engineering - Mission Critical & Secure Facilities to support our national Mission Critical and Secure Facilities practice, providing technical leadership for the design and execution of secure and classified facilities for U.S. federal, Department of War, and Intelligence Community clients.

This role is focused on the technical implementation of ICD 705, SCIF, SAPF, Open Storage Secret (OSS), TEMPEST, and related security requirements, translating security criteria into coordinated, constructible architectural and engineering solutions, construction documents, specifications, and technical details.

The successful candidate will serve as a technical liaison between government security stakeholders and multidisciplinary project teams and possess a strong understanding of how physical and technical security requirements integrate with architectural, engineering, telecommunications, audiovisual, electronic security, and other building systems. The position will support projects throughout both CONUS and OCONUS locations.

Key Responsibilities include but are not limited to:

• Serve as a technical lead for secure facility design and execution, interpreting and applying ICD 705, SCIF, SAPF, OSS, TEMPEST, and related physical and technical security criteria.
• Translate security requirements into coordinated design criteria, construction documents, specifications, technical details, and constructible solutions.
• Lead multidisciplinary coordination with architects, engineers, technology and security specialists, contractors, and government stakeholders, including SSMs, SSOs, CTTAs, and Accrediting Officials.
• Develop and review technical solutions for secure perimeter construction, doors and openings, penetrations, acoustic protection, access control, intrusion detection, and other physical security requirements.
• Coordinate TEMPEST and RF mitigation strategies, including RF shielding, non-conductive breaks, waveguide-below-cutoff penetrations, power and signal filtering, grounding/bonding, and related countermeasures.
• Conduct existing-condition surveys, facility assessments, and feasibility studies for new construction, renovation, conversion, and upgrade of secure environments.
• Perform technical design, interdisciplinary coordination, quality-control, and constructability reviews to ensure security requirements are appropriately incorporated into project documentation.
• Provide technical support during construction, including review of submittals, RFIs, shop drawings, field conditions, inspections, testing, and resolution of security-related issues, and support accreditation/certification and project closeout as applicable.
• Support development and implementation of secure facility standards, specifications, details, tools, and best practices, while maintaining awareness of evolving government security criteria.
• Support proposal development, technical approaches, scopes of work, and strategic growth opportunities for the Mission Critical and Secure Facilities practice.

Successful candidates will demonstrate the following critical qualifications and capabilities:

• Demonstrated experience interpreting and implementing ICD 705, SCIF, SAPF, OSS, TEMPEST, and related secure facility requirements.
• Demonstrated ability to translate security requirements into construction drawings, specifications, technical details, and multidisciplinary design solutions.
• Knowledge of secure perimeter construction and RF/TEMPEST mitigation techniques, including penetrations, shielding, non-conductive breaks, waveguide-below-cutoff protection, and power/signal filtering.
• Strong understanding of multidisciplinary building systems and their interaction with physical and technical security requirements.
• Experience with secure facility assessments, technical design reviews, and construction-phase support.
• Strong technical leadership, coordination, written communication, and presentation skills.
• Ability and willingness to travel periodically in support of CONUS and OCONUS projects.

Minimum Requirements

• Bachelor's degree in Engineering or a related building design or technical discipline and 10+ years including two years of leadership, of professional experience, including significant experience with federal secure, classified, or mission-critical facilities or demonstrated equivalency of experience and/or education.
• Professional registration appropriate to the candidate's discipline, such as Registered Architect (RA), or comparable professional credential.
• Ability to pass drug, and background checks to work on Federal grounds, military installations, and school grounds.
• This position requires U.S. citizenship due to federal contract/security requirements.

Preferred Qualifications

• 15+ years of professional experience, including 5+ years focused on SCIF, SAPF, TEMPEST, OSS, or comparable secure/classified facilities.
• Advanced experience with the design, documentation, construction, inspection, and accreditation/certification of secure facilities.
• Completion of recognized training related to ICD 705, SCIF/SAPF design and construction, TEMPEST, RF shielding, or related secure facility criteria.
• Experience working directly with SSMs, SSOs, CTTAs, Accrediting Officials, and other government security authorities.
• Experience developing secure facility standards, specifications, standard details, design guides, or quality-control procedures.
• Experience supporting secure facility projects in both CONUS and OCONUS locations.
• Experience with Autodesk Revit and BIM-based multidisciplinary coordination.
• Active U.S. Government security clearance, or demonstrated ability to obtain and maintain a security clearance.

jobs.description:
The Microbiology Department Project Lead serves as the technical leader for a sterile pharmaceutical manufacturing site, overseeing microbiological testing, environmental monitoring, contamination control, laboratory operations, projects, change controls, GMP documentation, method qualification and validation, investigations, deviations, and CAPAs.  The role also coordinates with cross-functional partners, assesses microbiological risks, drives continuous improvement, monitors regulatory and scientific developments, supports inspections and audits, analyzes data and trends, manages project resources, and mentors personnel while championing scientific excellence, compliance, and operational effectiveness.

For a Microbiology Department Project Lead role supporting a sterile pharmaceutical manufacturing site, you can position the role as the technical leader responsible for microbiology program governance, laboratory projects, and quality system improvements.

Key Responsibilities

• Serve as the technical lead for the Microbiology department, providing scientific oversight and guidance for microbiological testing, environmental monitoring, contamination control, and laboratory operations.
• Lead and manage microbiology-related projects from initiation through implementation, ensuring alignment with business objectives, regulatory requirements, and site priorities.
• Own and coordinate microbiology change controls, assessing technical impact, defining implementation strategies, and ensuring timely closure of quality records.
• Author, review, approve, and implement microbiology procedures, specifications, protocols, and technical documents to maintain compliance with current GMP requirements.
• Lead method qualification, verification, validation, and transfer activities for microbiological and rapid microbiological methods.
• Provide technical review and approval of investigations, deviations, laboratory events, and CAPAs related to microbiological processes and testing.
• Partner with Quality Assurance, Manufacturing, Engineering, Validation, and Regulatory Affairs to support product and process changes, new product introductions, and operational improvements.
• Assess microbiological risks associated with process changes, equipment modifications, facility upgrades, and contamination control strategies.
• Drive continuous improvement initiatives to enhance laboratory efficiency, data integrity, compliance, and contamination control effectiveness.
• Monitor and interpret emerging regulatory expectations, industry standards, and scientific advancements to ensure microbiology programs remain compliant and inspection-ready.
• Support regulatory inspections and customer audits by serving as the microbiology subject matter expert and presenting technical justifications, data, and program strategies.
• Analyze microbiological data and trends to identify risks, improve process understanding, and recommend actions that strengthen product quality and patient safety.
• Coordinate cross-functional teams to ensure successful execution of microbiology projects, timelines, deliverables, and resource planning.

Preferred Leadership Responsibilities

• Act as the primary microbiology SME for technical decision-making and strategic laboratory initiatives.
• Mentor microbiologists and laboratory personnel on scientific principles, regulatory expectations, and best practices.
• Champion a culture of scientific excellence, compliance, continuous improvement, and operational effectiveness within the Microbiology organization.

• Bachelor’s degree in Science/Engineering/Business Management or equivalent technical work experience
• 5+ years of relevant Quality experience in a GMP pharmaceutical, biologics, and/or medical device manufacturing environment
• Strong understanding of cGxPs, regulatory inspections, regulatory documents, global regulations, and standards
• Experience in Project Management and leading cross-functional project teams with technical professionals in a global and/or complex, matrixed organization
• Strong oral and written communication, interpersonal, time management, influence, and problem-solving skills

jobs.title: Treatment Operator
jobs.description:
Position Purpose:

Maintains water production and quality for public consumption. Monitors daily system demand along with influencing factors such as weather and seasonality. Controls system pressure, monitors booster stations and storage facilities, and observes treatment conditions. Operates and maintains water treatment plants and well systems to support a Class IV water system. Operates on-site and using Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition systems and other technology in the most efficient manner. Performs basic troubleshooting, installation, maintenance, and repair of mechanical, electrical, pumping and other equipment and facilities associated with water production, treatment and control. System operates 24-7 and during peak season, Treatment Operators working in the plants will be required to cover shift work as needed or assigned.

Primary Duties/Responsibilities:

• Conducting routine water testing and recording test results.
• Monitoring all charts, gauges, digital screens, and other operating equipment.
• Calculating the chemical feed rate required, calibrating feed equipment, and adjusting feed rate per lab tests or supervisor instructions.
• Performing and recording routine and special installation, maintenance and/or repair of all equipment and grounds and maintaining good housekeeping procedures.
• Analyzing system parameters and determining when additional help is required (e.g. a main break).
• Monitoring appropriate chemical inventory levels.
• Operating water treatment plants, wells and ancillary equipment using SCADA control interfaces.
• Takes direction from company water quality personnel regarding water sampling, schedules, handling and the like.
• Perform basic troubleshooting, installation, maintenance, and repair of mechanical, electrical, pumping and other equipment and facilities associated with water production, treatment and control.
• Uses digital tools, (computer, laptop, tablet, smart phone, etc.) devices and software to communicate, and perform and record work.
• Other duties as assigned.
• Taking various shift assignments and on-call duty on a regular, rotational basis.
• Perform all job responsibilities and duties in compliance with all safety, health, environmental, and security laws, rules, policies, programs and training.

Work Environment:

• Work outside in all kinds of weather.
• These employees work indoors on concrete constantly and outdoors frequently, (outdoor conditions can be wet, muddy and slippery with extremes of heat and cold temperatures).

Education/Experience/Background:

• High School Diploma/GED is required.
• Previous experience in water production and/or water treatment operation roles preferred.

Knowledge/Skills/Abilities:

jobs.title: Secure Facilities Technical Design - Mission Critical & Secure Facilities
jobs.description:
AECOM is seeking an experienced Secure Facilities Technical Design - Mission Critical & Secure Facilities to support our national Mission Critical and Secure Facilities practice, providing technical leadership for the design and execution of secure and classified facilities for U.S. federal, Department of War, and Intelligence Community clients.

This role is focused on the technical implementation of ICD 705, SCIF, SAPF, Open Storage Secret (OSS), TEMPEST, and related security requirements, translating security criteria into coordinated, constructible architectural and engineering solutions, construction documents, specifications, and technical details.

The successful candidate will serve as a technical liaison between government security stakeholders and multidisciplinary project teams and possess a strong understanding of how physical and technical security requirements integrate with architectural, engineering, telecommunications, audiovisual, electronic security, and other building systems. The position will support projects throughout both CONUS and OCONUS locations.

Key Responsibilities include but are not limited to:

• Serve as a technical lead for secure facility design and execution, interpreting and applying ICD 705, SCIF, SAPF, OSS, TEMPEST, and related physical and technical security criteria.
• Translate security requirements into coordinated design criteria, construction documents, specifications, technical details, and constructible solutions.
• Lead multidisciplinary coordination with architects, engineers, technology and security specialists, contractors, and government stakeholders, including SSMs, SSOs, CTTAs, and Accrediting Officials.
• Develop and review technical solutions for secure perimeter construction, doors and openings, penetrations, acoustic protection, access control, intrusion detection, and other physical security requirements.
• Coordinate TEMPEST and RF mitigation strategies, including RF shielding, non-conductive breaks, waveguide-below-cutoff penetrations, power and signal filtering, grounding/bonding, and related countermeasures.
• Conduct existing-condition surveys, facility assessments, and feasibility studies for new construction, renovation, conversion, and upgrade of secure environments.
• Perform technical design, interdisciplinary coordination, quality-control, and constructability reviews to ensure security requirements are appropriately incorporated into project documentation.
• Provide technical support during construction, including review of submittals, RFIs, shop drawings, field conditions, inspections, testing, and resolution of security-related issues, and support accreditation/certification and project closeout as applicable.
• Support development and implementation of secure facility standards, specifications, details, tools, and best practices, while maintaining awareness of evolving government security criteria.
• Support proposal development, technical approaches, scopes of work, and strategic growth opportunities for the Mission Critical and Secure Facilities practice.

Successful candidates will demonstrate the following critical qualifications and capabilities:

• Demonstrated experience interpreting and implementing ICD 705, SCIF, SAPF, OSS, TEMPEST, and related secure facility requirements.
• Demonstrated ability to translate security requirements into construction drawings, specifications, technical details, and multidisciplinary design solutions.
• Knowledge of secure perimeter construction and RF/TEMPEST mitigation techniques, including penetrations, shielding, non-conductive breaks, waveguide-below-cutoff protection, and power/signal filtering.
• Strong understanding of multidisciplinary building systems and their interaction with physical and technical security requirements.
• Experience with secure facility assessments, technical design reviews, and construction-phase support.
• Strong technical leadership, coordination, written communication, and presentation skills.
• Ability and willingness to travel periodically in support of CONUS and OCONUS projects.

Minimum Requirements

• Bachelor's degree in Architecture or a related building design or technical discipline and 10+ years including two years of leadership, of professional experience, including significant experience with federal secure, classified, or mission-critical facilities or demonstrated equivalency of experience and/or education.
• Professional registration appropriate to the candidate's discipline, such as Registered Architect (RA), or comparable professional credential.
• Ability to pass drug, and background checks to work on Federal grounds, military installations, and school grounds.
• This position requires U.S. citizenship due to federal contract/security requirements.

Preferred Qualifications

• 15+ years of professional experience, including 5+ years focused on SCIF, SAPF, TEMPEST, OSS, or comparable secure/classified facilities.
• Advanced experience with the design, documentation, construction, inspection, and accreditation/certification of secure facilities.
• Completion of recognized training related to ICD 705, SCIF/SAPF design and construction, TEMPEST, RF shielding, or related secure facility criteria.
• Experience working directly with SSMs, SSOs, CTTAs, Accrediting Officials, and other government security authorities.
• Experience developing secure facility standards, specifications, standard details, design guides, or quality-control procedures.
• Experience supporting secure facility projects in both CONUS and OCONUS locations.
• Experience with Autodesk Revit and BIM-based multidisciplinary coordination.
• Active U.S. Government security clearance, or demonstrated ability to obtain and maintain a security clearance.

jobs.title: High School Science Teacher
jobs.description:
Uncommon High School Science teachers work collaboratively across the network to prepare all students with the tools and knowledge to critically engage in the field of science and develop them into self-directed learners. At the heart of all Science courses is inquiry-based learning, including a robust focus on student discourse and the science practices. Science teachers employ a variety of instructional strategies to develop a passion for scientific questioning and analysis in their students. Our teachers prepare all students such that they have the choice to study and excel in any STEM discipline. We prepare all students to be citizen scientists that have the tools and knowledge to critically engage in the field of science regardless of their university major or professional career. Our teachers become experts in their course content and have a keen sense of how to motivate and inspire high school students.

Responsibilities

1.     Instruction

• You’ll teach a curriculum that includes, but is not limited to, analysis of Biology, Chemistry, Physics, and Environmental Sciences that prepares students for Advanced Placement (AP) and collegiate level coursework.
• You'll develop students’ practices skills of questioning, modeling, constructing explanations, data analysis, argumentation, and planning and conducting interactive labs.
• You’ll create an environment where students feel confident using their voice to engage in scientific discourse.
• You will facilitate student-led discourse, during which students use evidence to make sophisticated claims and synthesize and critique arguments.
• You'll facilitate student-led inquiry of various scientific topics and engage students in lab and project-based performance tasks.
• You'll work with the Science department to determine academic and engagement goals for students.

2.     Data Analysis

• You'll meet weekly with your principal and/or instructional coach to analyze and respond to trends in student work samples and assessments.
• You'll learn and implement strategies to differentiate instruction for all learners in your classroom.

3.     School Culture

• You’ll build positive relationships with students to ensure they feel seen, loved, and heard.
• You’ll partner with students’ families to ensure appropriate resources are available to support their child's learning needs.
• You'll engage in practice-based professional development, mentorship, and coaching sessions.
• You'll participate in weekly, school-wide meetings to cultivate community, model our core values, and encourage student achievement.
• You'll partner with your grade level team to develop academic goals and practice instructional strategies.

• A demonstrated commitment to supporting students’ social emotional and academic development
• An enthusiasm for collaborating with internal and external partners in the best interest of students
• A self-directed learner who solicits and implements feedback to improve outcomes and achieve objectives
• Required Experience:A demonstrated interest in impacting K-12 students in urban schools and communities (1-2 years experience preferred).Academic expertise in Science, Technology, Engineering, Mathematics, or other related fields of study. Prior to the start of employment, you must have a bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university. Teacher certification is not a prerequisite for consideration at Uncommon Schools in the state of NJ, but you do need to meet NJ state certification eligibility requirements (a final undergraduate or graduate cumulative GPA of 3.0 for graduates on or after 9/1/16, or 2.75 if you graduated prior to 9/1/16). All instructional staff are required to become certified in the state of New Jersey within a reasonable period after beginning employment.

jobs.title: High School Math Teacher
jobs.description:
Uncommon High School Math teachers work in grade teams and content teams to push students towards being self-guided learners. Our teachers become experts in their course content, and have a keen sense of how to motivate and inspire high school students. At the heart of all math classes is a deep joy for mathematics. Math teachers use a variety of instructional strategies to cultivate student awareness of how to make sense of, persevere through, and solve problems. At the conclusion of high school, students are prepared for academic autonomy and college preparatory work.

• You'll use a Math curriculum to teach content that may include Algebra, Geometry, or Calculus and prepares students for Advanced Placement (AP) and collegiate level coursework.
• You'll support students as they solve problems and think critically.
• You'll use your love of mathematics to foster confidence and meaningful engagement with the subject for students.
• You'll cultivate the ability to construct and justify viable arguments using reasoning, math vocabulary, tools, and postulates.
• You'll use your passion for mathematics to build a community of self-guided learners where students feel safe, confident, and engaged.
• You'll work with the Math department to determine academic and engagement goals for students.

2.     Data Analysis

• You'll meet weekly with your principal and/or instructional coach to analyze and respond to trends in student work samples and assessments.

• You’ll build positive relationships with students to ensure they feel seen, loved, and heard.

Responsibilities:

• Supports and enables the delivery of quality patient care service.
• Directs, prioritizes, and adjusts staff work assignments for assigned shift to ensure timely and accurate delivery of Operating Room (OR) equipment, supplies, and case carts.
• Assigns staff to job duties to meet the demands of patient care areas, patient volume, trauma emergencies, and staff vacancies.
• May interact with various hospital departments, physician’s offices, and outside vendors to effectively assist in the management of department operations.
• Promotes a positive first impression with department and clinic personnel, vendor representatives, and guests, establishing a role as resource for end-users.
• Encourages teamwork and effective communication with staff, promoting the philosophy and objectives of NM and department. Serves as a resource to staff and end-users.

• Helps identify strengths and weaknesses of employees to properly assess employee growth throughout the year. May provide performance and productivity feedback to the Sterile Processing Manager for performance evaluations.
• Identifies and assesses learning needs related to processes and procedures including decontamination, assembly, sterilization, inventory storage, and OR case cart distribution.
• Assists with educational offerings, policy reviews and revision, competencies, quality assurance, and daily rounds.
• Develops, promotes, and encourages staff education and certification, and assists in the orientation and training of new and existing staff.
• Performs daily OR and Sterile Processing rounds, including audits of documentation, and accuracy of case cart instrument and supply requirements. Documents and reports findings.
• Performs daily OR and Sterile Processing audits of decontamination equipment testing results and sterilization records/printouts. Documents and reports findings. Stores according to department policy.
• Coordinates instrument processing and turnaround activities and workflow. Communicates with OR and vendor representatives as needed.
• Monitors utilization of supplies and equipment for optimal efficiency, cost containment, and timely reordering of instruments, fracture implants, robotic supplies, department supplies, and recycling programs.
• Maintains communication board and instructions for use files.
• May act as the liaison between OR and Sterile Processing.
• Assists with the selection of new team members.
• Works with OR to develop and revise instrument trays and orders instruments as needed.
• Assists in the management and coordination of new instrument reviews, purchases, instrument replacement, instrument refurbishment, and instrument repairs. Maintains documentation.
• Maintains the instrument tracking system including the building and revision of instrument count sheets.
• Monitors loaner instrumentation/equipment requests and reprocessing.
• Coordinate with NM Materials Management in inventory control and in the evaluation and procurement of new product requests. Assists with recycling programs.
• Reports instances of equipment irregularities and failure as soon as possible and coordinates service/maintenance follow-up as needed.
• Assists in reviewing and updating policies and procedures for content and accuracy; makes necessary changes; and in the enforcement of policies and procedures
• Maintains communication board and assists in the review and update of the manufacturers’ instructions for use. Assists in providing guidance for new and one-time use items.
• Ensure all work areas and equipment are cleaned and maintained according to Infection Control standards and to ensure a safe work environment. Comply with regulatory, Environmental, Safety, Hazardous Materials, and Infection Control policies and procedures.
• Assist in orientation of new employees to each work assignment area and total department operation. Complete the required orientation documentation for new employees assigned to the shift. Provide feedback regarding progress of employees. Provide input to Manager regarding staff Annual Performance Management Review and/or Action Plan.
• Other duties as assigned.

Required:

• High School diploma or equivalent
• Certification from either CBSPD or IAHCSMM. Maintains certification.
• Five years or more experience in a Sterile Processing Department
• Experience and knowledge of surgical instrumentation
• Knowledge and understanding of Human Anatomy and Physiology, Medical Terminology, basic microbiology, and a variety of OR surgical procedures
• Minimum of one year supervisory or coordinator experience in Sterile Processing or related field.
• Good verbal and written communication skills
• Basic computer skills

jobs.description:
HOW YOU WILL MAKE AN IMPACT

The Compliance & Privacy Officer will support key elements of the Company’s compliance program including our Code of Conduct, Business Ethics, compliance risk assessments, policies and procedures, internal controls and other compliance initiatives.

The position is also accountable for the US & Canada privacy program, ensuring compliance with evolving privacy laws and embedding privacy requirements into business processes, third party relationships, and AI initiatives.

The successful candidate will possess strong analytical skills, sound judgment on sensitive matters, and the ability to effectively communicate compliance guidance while partnering with stakeholders across the global organization. The position is well suited for someone who thrives in a complex, international compliance environment.

Compliance Program

• Support day-to-day compliance activities related to conflicts of interest, external business activities, gifts and hospitality, and sponsorships.
• Promote and reinforce a culture of integrity, ethical business conduct, accountability, and regulatory compliance across the organization.
• Support implementation and monitoring of compliance requirements related to anti-corruption, antitrust, anti-money laundering – AML and business ethics.
• Regionalize and deliver compliance training materials and policy updates to maintain a high standard of awareness across the workforce.
• Assist in the refinement and maintenance of the company’s compliance policies, procedures, and governance frameworks.
• Proactively identify compliance risks, process improvements, opportunities to drive issues through resolution, and effective risk-based compliance and privacy controls.
• Monitor legislative, regulatory, and enforcement developments and translate them into clear, practical guidance for the business.
• Keep abreast of developments in compliance, ethics, privacy, data protection, AI governance, and related regulatory requirements, and proactively advise the business on emerging risks, trends, and compliance obligations.

Data Privacy Advisory

• Advise on compliance with global, federal, and state under applicable U.S. and Canadian privacy laws, including GDPR, CCPA/CPRA, and VCDPA, and other emerging regulations.
• Draft, review, and negotiate data protection agreements (DPAs), privacy terms, vendor contracts, and cross‑border data transfer mechanisms.
• Collaborate closely with Information and Cyber Security and IT teams on incident response, including breach assessment, notification obligations, regulatory reporting, risk mitigation remediation strategies, and continuous improvement of incident management processes.
• Lead and support the development, implementation and ongoing maintenance of privacy governance documentation, including records of processing activities, data inventories, privacy policies, internal procedures, data retention schedules, and related governance frameworks.
• Conduct Privacy Impact Assessments (PIAs), data mapping, and privacy risk evaluations for new products, technologies, systems, AI solutions, vendors and business initiatives, ensuring that privacy-by-design principles and regulatory requirements are effectively integrated into business operations.
• Provide legal guidance on data collection, use, retention, and sharing, including consent, cookies, and marketing practices.
• Monitor and interpret evolving privacy laws and regulatory guidance; develop and delivery privacy awareness and training for internal stakeholders.

jobs.description:

jobs.title: Principal Fellow
jobs.description:
To build more high-performing schools, we need leaders to commit themselves to the most urgent and exciting work of our time. Uncommon Schools Principal Fellows are strategically trained and developed using best-in-class practices with the goal of stepping into an Uncommon Principal role upon completion of the Fellowship, in which they will co-lead a school alongside an Uncommon Director of Operations. This Principal Fellow and eventual Principal is a full-time employee, hired, supported, and evaluated by the Regional Superintendent of Instruction and the Senior Director of School Support.  The fellowship is based on a foundation of core elements aligned to the competencies of Uncommon Principals. Each element is designed to build Principal Fellows’ capacity towards becoming effective instructional school leaders:

Feedback and Assessment

Feedback, especially individualized feedback, is the main tool that will support the Principal Fellow’s growth as a leader and is the main reason our schools go from good to great. Principal Fellows will receive feedback formally and informally throughout the Fellowship during their time in schools, professional development, and in cross-regional Fellow cohort gatherings. This will include feedback from the Principal Fellow’s Host Principal, the Regional Superintendent of Instruction, and the Senior Director of School Support.

School Immersion

By integrating fully into the day-to-day activities of an Uncommon school, Principal Fellows will gain exposure to situations they may face as a school leader and be challenged to manage the complexity of scenarios that occur at a school.  Principal Fellows will work with their Host Principal and the Senior Director of School Support throughout their Fellowship to plan how they will master the skills and competencies needed to lead a high-performing school, including Instructional Leadership, Teacher Development, School Culture, and Family Engagement. Principal Fellows are “in the driver’s seat” of their learning and must seek and plan for opportunities throughout their Fellowship to demonstrate a leadership presence and readiness to lead while being fully immersed within a school.

Professional Development

Principal Fellows join our Principals in monthly, cross-regional professional development. This is an important opportunity to learn alongside Principals and cohort members about the most up-to-date instructional leadership and people management best practices to develop your leadership capabilities.

In addition, Principal Fellows will attend a series of cohort-specific professional development workshops which are more intimate and allow for more “at-bats,” practice and direct application to their school immersion. These cohort sessions will provide opportunities for Principal Fellows to look to one another for professional and personal support.

• Passionate commitment to the mission of Uncommon Schools;
• Passionate commitment to expand knowledge, skills, and opportunities for students both in and out of school;
• Dedication to building culturally responsive learning partnerships with students, teachers, and families;
• Demonstrates tenacity, personal responsibility, a founder’s mentality, and a commitment to continual professional growth;
• Strong people management skills, including the ability to effectively navigate difficult conversations and hold staff, scholars, and families accountable in a supportive manner;
• Ability to develop and maintain a strong staff culture that is clearly focused on realizing our Uncommon mission;
• Strong data analysis skills;
• Ability to provide high-leverage feedback via classroom observations;
• Ability to strategically manage and prioritize time and tasks effectively to fully meet the needs of their school, with a lens toward systems thinking;
• Ability to thrive in a fast-paced environment; flexible, able to work autonomously and take direction as needed;
• Familiarity and success with–or commitment to–implementing Uncommon’s core tenets of instructional leadership (e.g., See It-Name It-Do It framework, Leverage Leadership principles);
• Required experience:At least 3 years of teaching experience with evidence of outstanding student growth and achievement;At least 1 year of experience coaching, leading, and/or managing teachers (e.g., Assistant Principal, Dean of Curriculum, Instructional Leader, grade level chair, content/department chair);Experience teaching core subjects (e.g., Math, ELA, Science, History) is preferred.A Bachelor's degree.

Our people are what make us Uncommon. We offer competitive compensation and comprehensive benefits that support the personal health, wellness, and finances of our staff and their families. Our compensation philosophy values equity & fairness and attracting & retaining top talent.

Our Approach to AI and Your Application

At Uncommon Schools, we value thoughtful use of technology. Your responses should begin with your own thinking and reflect your authentic voice, experiences, and commitment to our mission. Generative AI can be used to refine or organize writing, but not to generate initial responses or replace your ideas. Every application is reviewed by a member of our Recruitment Team, and we are committed to understanding the person behind the application.

Compensation

Compensation for this role is between $103,000 to $109,300. Most candidates who meet job description requirements will receive an offer of $103,000.

Starting pay is determined using various factors including but not limited to relevant professional development, education certifications, and tenure with Uncommon Schools.

Product Lifecycle Management

Roadmap & Backlog Ownership

Stakeholder Engagement & Requirements Gathering

jobs.title: Pre-K Teacher
jobs.description:
Uncommon Pre-K Teachers cultivate a love for learning in every student from the very start. Teachers and students engage in an environment that fosters curiosity, achievement, respect, and empathy (CARE). Our classrooms are engaging, intentional, and playful, and our educators encourage core values of respect and hard work while celebrating each child’s individuality. Through this work, teachers lay the academic and social-emotional foundations that carry students to and through college. Pre-K classrooms are led by teaching teams that include a lead teacher and an apprentice teacher.

Responsibilities

1. Instruction

• You’ll co-teach and build an engaging and joyful classroom environment that encourages mastery and empowers students to learn through exploration and purposeful play.
• You’ll teach literacy (reading comprehension, phonics, language development, vocabulary, and writing), mathematics, and core knowledge (science and social studies).
• You’ll collaborate with the teaching team (lead & apprentice teachers) to facilitate free-choice centers and small group instruction.

2. Data Analysis

• You’ll meet weekly with your Director to analyze and respond to trends in student work samples and assessments.
• You’ll learn and implement strategies to differentiate instruction for all learners in your classroom.

3. Classroom Culture

• You’ll implement Uncommon’s instructional model and collaborate with the instructional coach and Director to ensure students meet academic and performance goals.
• You’ll use multiple data sources, including assessments and classroom quality observations, to make day-to-day instructional decisions (reflective).
• You’ll provide early learning experiences that foster positive feelings about school, teachers, and the broader community (nurturing).
• You’ll support student development across social-emotional, physical, cognitive, and academic domains (balanced).
• You’ll apply a variety of strategies to promote both conceptual understanding and skill development.
• You’ll model and support expressive and receptive language development throughout the school day.
• You’ll support administrative and operational tasks, including document creation, office support, and responding to student send-outs.
• You’ll assist with behavior interventions, student supervision, and accurate record-keeping to maintain a safe, structured, and positive learning environment.

4. School Culture

• You’ll provide classroom coverage as needed to ensure continuity of instruction and supervision.
• You’ll build strong, positive relationships with students so they feel seen, valued, and supported.
• You’ll partner with families to ensure appropriate resources are in place to support student learning and development.
• You’ll engage in practice-based professional development, mentorship, and coaching.
• You’ll support daily school operations including morning arrival, lunch duty, student assemblies, transitions, and after-school dismissal.
• You’ll participate in weekly school-wide meetings to foster community, model core values, and support student achievement.
• You’ll collaborate with teaching partners and grade-level teams to set academic goals and strengthen instructional practice.

• A demonstrated commitment to supporting students’ social emotional and academic development
• An enthusiasm for working with families in the best interest of students

The successful candidate will help ensure compliance with applicable competition laws while providing practical, business-oriented legal guidance in a complex and evolving regulatory environment.

jobs.title: High School Athletic Director
jobs.description:
The Athletic Director leads, manages, and executes all aspects of the North Star High School athletic program. The Athletic Director is responsible for fostering a culture of academic and athletic excellence, ensuring compliance and safety, managing operational logistics, supporting student-athlete development, and leading coaching staff.

Responsibilities

1. Department Leadership & Vision

• Mission Alignment: Develop, articulate, and enforce a clear, ambitious mission statement for school athletics that aligns with the academic mission of the school and sets clear expectations for coaches, student-athletes, parents, and the community.
• Innovation & Continuous Improvement: Implement high-leverage innovations within the athletic department to dramatically improve student performance while preserving and enhancing the school’s core values.

2. Student, Family, & Coaching Staff Management

• Department Culture: Foster a respectful, highly collaborative environment where students and coaches demonstrate leadership. Model asset-based thinking through praise, aspiration, and positive behavior reinforcement.
• Academic Monitoring & Support: Establish systems to monitor the academic achievement of all student-athletes. Partner with coaches, teachers, Special Education Coordinators, social workers to support students with IEPs, BIPs, 504 plans, and English Language Learners.
• Coach Recruitment & Development: Recruit, select, and retain highly qualified coaching staff. Provide ongoing feedback, ensure practices meet school standards, and conduct formal end-of-season evaluations.
• Family Engagement: Proactively communicate program schedules, deadlines, and key updates to families. Respond to family inquiries within 24 hours.
• K-16 Pipeline & Pathways: Collaborate with middle school leaders and coaches to create seamless transitions to high school athletics. Work with the College Placement team to ensure student-athletes are on track for post-secondary and collegiate athletic opportunities.

3. Operations, Logistics, & Compliance

• Budget & Financial Management: Develop, monitor, and manage the athletic budget in alignment with school priorities. Ensure timely payments to officials, facilities, and vendors, and actively pursue fundraising opportunities to support program needs.
• Systems & Safety: Ensure all student-athletes obtain physicals and required paperwork prior to participation. Design and execute comprehensive safety and security plans for home events in coordination with security and athletic trainers.
• Media & Digital Presence: Build, elevate, and manage a dynamic, engaging, and highly organized media presence. Maintain up-to-date, accurate program information on the athletic website and leverage social media platforms to highlight student-athlete accomplishments, promote upcoming events, foster community engagement, and strengthen school spirit.
• Scheduling & Transportation: Schedule rigorous, appropriate competition seasons and oversee timely transportation/bus scheduling. Promptly inform all stakeholders of schedule modifications or cancellations.
• Public Relations & Event Management: Cultivate a sportsmanlike, welcoming atmosphere for visiting teams and patrons.
• Compliance & Governance: Maintain accurate eligibility records according to school and state standards. Enforce state, conference, district, and school regulations, manage coach certifications, and represent the school at state and county association meetings.

4. Professionalism & School Contributions

• Whole-School Leadership: Maintain positive, collaborative relationships with colleagues and actively participate in whole-school events and initiatives.
