jobs.title: GTM Lead
jobs.location: Washington, District of Columbia, United States
jobs.description:
Grassroots Analytics (“GA”) is a political tech company dedicated to breaking down barriers in fundraising for progressive campaigns and causes. To facilitate that work, GA maintains a detailed database on more than 20 million active, left-leaning American donors, including data on net worth, ideological preferences, political donation history, non-profit donation history, demographics, and contact information. Our overall mission is to use that data to amplify forward-thinking voices, causes, and people.

Grassroots Analytics is seeking a GTM Lead to join our team. The GTM Lead will collaborate closely with the Director of GTM and Product team to support campaigns and organizations through client onboarding and success, education and enablement, and outbound and conference-driven sales coordination.

This role is ideal for someone passionate about client relationships, digital fundraising strategy, and helping clients get the most out of GA's platform.

Responsibilities

Customer Success & Retention (35%)

• Own the client success lifecycle from onboarding through long-term retention, ensuring clients understand and maximize the value of GA's product suite.

• Serve as the primary point of contact for client support needs, resolving issues directly and escalating complex cases to the appropriate team.

• Track client health and satisfaction, proactively flagging churn risk and identifying expansion opportunities.

Client Education & Enablement (25%)

• Build and run webinars, trainings, and onboarding sessions that help clients adopt new features and best practices.

• Develop and maintain help videos, guides, and other self-serve resources that reduce support burden and improve client self-sufficiency.

• Translate product updates into clear, client-facing education content.

Email Outreach & Sales Coordination (25%)

• Own GA's product communications — strategy, execution, and performance measurement (open/response/conversion rates).

• Coordinate the logistics and pipeline for conference-driven and outbound sales efforts — managing scheduling, follow-up systems, and lead handoff — in partnership with the Revenue team.

• Continuously refine outreach messaging and targeting based on performance data.

Cross-Functional Product Feedback (15%)

• Synthesize client feedback, support trends, and market objections into actionable input for the Product team.

• Partner with the Director of GTM to refine positioning, messaging, and onboarding materials based on what's working (and what isn't) with clients.

• Represent the voice of the client in cross-functional planning conversations.

The Grassroots Approach

At Grassroots Analytics, our work is guided by the following principles:

• Customer service is our core: Clients are always, without exception, treated with the highest level of professionalism and respect.

• We model a high bar for performance: We operate with the best interests of both the organization and every client in mind.

• We strengthen relationships at every level: Our "people first" approach builds trust with team members and clients alike.

• Proactivity drives problem-solving: We look at the big picture to develop solutions, anticipate challenges, and prevent future setbacks.

• Flexibility is essential: We adapt quickly as events change, take advantage of unexpected opportunities, and act decisively when needed.

Qualifications

The ideal candidate for the GTM Lead position will:

• Have at least 3 years of experience across client success, account management, and/or client-facing digital strategy roles.

• Have experience building and delivering client education content (e.g. webinars, trainings, video guides, or documentation).

• Have experience owning an email marketing or outreach channel, including writing copy and reporting on performance.

• Be comfortable coordinating cross-functional logistics (e.g. conference and outbound sales pipelines) without always being the one executing the pitch.

jobs.title: Audit Policy Analyst, Post-Acute Services
jobs.description:
Machinify is a leading healthcare intelligence company with expertise across the payment continuum, delivering unmatched value, transparency, and efficiency to health plan clients across the country. Deployed by over 85 health plans, including many of the top 20, and representing more than 270 million lives, Machinify brings together a fully configurable and content-rich, AI-powered platform along with best-in-class expertise. We’re constantly reimagining what’s possible in our industry, creating disruptively simple, powerfully clear ways to maximize financial outcomes and drive down healthcare costs.

As part of the Complex Payment Solutions (CPS) Team, the Audit Policy Analyst, Post-Acute Services serves as the subject matter expert for durable medical equipment (DME), home health, and home infusion therapy claims across government and commercial lines of business. This role leads the development, maintenance, testing, and optimization of post-acute payment integrity audit concepts and partners with operations, clinical, client services, and technology teams to ensure each concept is built, validated, and maintained in alignment with coding standards, coverage and medical necessity criteria, documentation requirements, and client-specific payer policy.

The ideal candidate brings authoritative, hands-on knowledge of how post-acute services are ordered, documented, billed, and paid, including DME MAC policy, the Home Health Patient-Driven Groupings Model (PDGM), and the Medicare home infusion therapy benefit. This role requires strong analytical and communication skills, a track record of leading audit concept development, the ability to manage complex workflows independently, and the ability to mentor a team of subject matter experts.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

Policy Development and Maintenance

• Develop new post-acute audit concepts for DME, home health, and home infusion therapy claims, including research, data and claim analysis, rule documents, and code lists.

• Review and update existing audit concepts on required periodic cycles or in response to client or regulatory changes, including quarterly HCPCS updates, DMEPOS fee schedule updates, and annual Home Health PPS final rules.

• Monitor and interpret changes to National Coverage Determinations (NCDs), DME MAC Local Coverage Determinations (LCDs) and Policy Articles, the Medicare Benefit Policy and Claims Processing Manuals, and CMS transmittals, and document their impact on existing concepts.

• Interpret and apply client-specific commercial and Medicaid payer policy, including home infusion per diem billing, DME rental and purchase rules, and prior authorization requirements.

• Approach for Medicaid audit development in DME and Home Health across multiple states and managed care contracts, the audit program should be built around both federal requirements and state-specific contract obligations.

Policy Testing and Validation

• Perform QA reviews of audit concepts to confirm compliance with regulatory, coding, and citation changes and to confirm updates are applied timely.

• Validate concept logic against post-acute billing rules, including DME capped rental and oxygen payment rules, modifier requirements (e.g., KX, GA, GZ, RR, NU, UE), home health 30-day period and LUPA logic, and home infusion therapy visit and drug billing.

• Identify discrepancies in concept performance and drive resolution with clinical, coding, and operations teams.

• Ensure audit concepts are validated against current coding guidelines, payment methodologies, and payer policy prior to deployment.

Operational and Workflow Support

• Manage, track, and progress multiple tasks across concurrent audit concept workflows with a high degree of accuracy and quality, delivering results on time.

• Ensure audit teams apply post-acute policies consistently and correctly across auditing platforms and client programs.

• Serve as the escalation point for auditors and clinical reviewers on complex DMEPOS, home health, and home infusion documentation and coverage questions.

Training and Documentation

• Create training materials, job aids, and reference tools for new and existing post-acute audit concepts, including documentation checklists for orders, face-to-face encounters, proof of delivery, homebound status, and plans of care.

• Maintain organized, accessible documentation of post-acute audit policies and concept updates.

Cross-Functional Collaboration and Client Support

• Respond to client inquiries and provide subject matter support to client services for presentations, provider disputes, and escalations involving post-acute claims.

• Partner with operations, clinical teams, technology, and internal stakeholders to support policy execution and drive concept quality.

• Provide expert feedback to improve policy usability, accuracy, and effectiveness across the organization.

Performance Monitoring and Analytics

• Monitor concept performance and provide statistical analysis to drive scoring and selection for new and existing post-acute audit concepts.

• Identify trends in DME, home health, and home infusion claim data, such as utilization outliers, high-cost supply patterns, and billing inconsistencies across care settings, and recommend actions to optimize audit yield and accuracy.

Process Improvement

• Identify opportunities to improve audit concept workflows, documentation processes, and policy management practices.

• Support ongoing enhancements to concept tracking, QA processes, and cross-functional coordination.

Other Duties

• Perform additional responsibilities and ad hoc projects as assigned to meet business needs.

Job Requirements

Education and Experience

• Bachelor's degree in nursing, health administration, business, or a related field, or equivalent experience.

• Minimum 5+ years of progressive experience in DME, home health, and/or home infusion therapy, including direct experience in payment integrity, claims auditing, or provider-side billing and compliance.

• Equivalent experience of 3+ years in post-acute claims auditing and recovery auditing.

• Registered Nurse or Certified Coder holding a nationally recognized credential (RHIA, RHIT, AHIMA, AAPC, or equivalent) required.

• Home health coding (HCS-D, BCHH-C), OASIS (COS-C), or infusion nursing (CRNI) credential preferred.

Knowledge, Skills, and Expertise

• Demonstrated depth and breadth of knowledge across post-acute coding systems and payment methodologies, including ICD-10-CM, HCPCS Level II, CPT, and HIPPS, the DME fee schedule and Competitive Bidding Program, Home Health PPS under PDGM, and the Medicare home infusion therapy benefit.

• Deep understanding of DME MAC jurisdictions, LCDs, Policy Articles, and supplier documentation requirements, including Standard Written Orders, face-to-face encounters, proof of delivery, continued need, and the DME Required Prior Authorization List.

• Deep understanding of Medicare home health conditions of payment, including homebound status, face-to-face encounter, certification and recertification, plan of care, OASIS assessment, and the Notice of Admission.

• Broad knowledge of provider billing guidelines, payer reimbursement policies, medical necessity criteria, and claim adjudication standards for post-acute services.

• Expert knowledge of clinical documentation requirements and audit concept development for post-acute claim types.

• Strong experience in data utilization and statistical analysis, including driving scoring and selection for audit concepts.

• Progressive healthcare data analysis experience, including gathering and documenting requirements for projects of diverse scope and complexity.

• Experience developing clinical content, policy documentation, and training resources.

• Proven ability to communicate effectively with all levels of the organization, with diverse teams, and with external clients.

• Exceptional written and verbal communication skills with strong attention to detail.

• Excellent critical thinking and analytical skills.

• Demonstrated ability to manage multiple concurrent workflows independently and in a remote environment, delivering results on time.

Computer Equipment and Software

• Proficient in Windows office systems, including the full Microsoft Suite (Excel, Word, Outlook, PowerPoint, SharePoint, and Teams).

• Advanced skills in Microsoft Office, particularly Excel and PowerPoint.

• Familiarity with encoder and grouper applications, including the Home Health PDGM Grouper.

• Experience working with various software platforms and collaborating with development teams.

• Proven success in a remote working environment.

We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression, or veteran status. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace. Machinify is an employment at will employer. We participate in E-Verify as required by applicable law. About the Role
We’re hiring a Principal Software Engineer to help define and build the next generation of AI-powered software development workflows.


“Full stack” in this role extends well beyond traditional frontend and backend development. You will set technical direction and lead major product initiatives spanning user interfaces, developer tooling, workflow orchestration, agent and prompt design, backend systems, and cloud infrastructure.


This is a highly product-oriented technical leadership role. You will identify the highest-leverage opportunities across the software development lifecycle, turn ambiguous user and technical problems into durable product and system strategies, and lead execution across multiple engineers and partner teams. Your work will shape both the architecture of Codex and how developers around the world design, write, review, test, and maintain software.
You will operate as a senior individual contributor: remaining deeply involved in design and implementation while raising the technical judgment, execution quality, and ambition of the broader team.


In this role, you will

 - Set the technical and product direction for significant areas of Codex, translating an evolving product vision into scalable architectures and an actionable engineering strategy.

 - Lead complex, multi-quarter initiatives spanning client applications, backend services, agent systems, cloud infrastructure, and developer tooling.

 - Design AI-powered workflows that generalize across languages, codebases, development environments, and organizations while remaining intuitive, reliable, and safe.

 - Make high-consequence architectural decisions under ambiguity, balancing rapid product learning with long-term system quality and adaptability.

 - Identify opportunities that cut across existing team or product boundaries, align stakeholders around a direction, and drive the work from exploration through launch and iteration.

 - Partner closely with product, design, research, infrastructure, security, and go-to-market teams to turn emerging model capabilities and developer needs into coherent product experiences.

 - Work directly with developers, open-source maintainers, startups, and large enterprises to uncover unmet needs and distinguish foundational opportunities from incremental improvements.

 - Establish patterns and standards for reliability, observability, performance, experimentation, and evaluation across AI-powered developer workflows.

 - Serve as a technical multiplier by reviewing critical designs, mentoring engineers, improving engineering practices, and helping the team navigate its hardest product and technical decisions.

 - Contribute directly to implementation, particularly where the problem is novel, technically demanding, or requires connecting multiple layers of the product.

You might thrive in this role if you

 - Have led the design and delivery of technically complex, user-facing systems with impact extending beyond a single feature or team.

 - Combine deep software-engineering expertise with exceptional product judgment and can move fluently across product interfaces, distributed systems, infrastructure, and developer tooling.

 - Have a track record of creating clarity in ambiguous problem spaces, setting a compelling technical direction, and bringing multiple teams or disciplines along with you.

 - Remain hands-on while increasing the effectiveness of other engineers through architecture, mentorship, decision-making, and technical leadership.

 - Understand modern software-development workflows deeply and can recognize where AI agents require fundamentally new interaction and system designs.

 - Have experience building or operating AI-powered products and understand the challenges created by nondeterminism, evaluation, latency, reliability, safety, and rapidly evolving model capabilities.

Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE JOB

We are looking for Product Sourcing Engineer interns to join our rapidly growing teams. In this role, you will be responsible for driving the strategic supply network development and cost management of Anduril’s product hardware, across their lifecycles, by collaborating with suppliers and cross-functionally, including stakeholders in engineering, quality, and manufacturing.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

• Conduct supplier selection for a specific product, leveraging approved supplier list.

• Partner with strategic suppliers to accelerate product development via activities such as:

• Concept scoping to quickly solidify requirements

• Feature trade-off / trade tables

• Total Cost of Ownership modeling

• Joint design development, via clear statements of work

• Simulation of mechanical & electronics designs

• Develop and execute on sourcing strategy via full market knowledge, supplier rationalization, commodity pricing plan and effective principles to drive efficiency and cost

• Drive the development and consolidation of a manufacturing BOM, working with Quality & Manufacturing, to ramp production internally and with our suppliers with high flexibility

• Be accountable for all NPI component procurement, on-time and correctly, to scale up manufacturing operations

• Manage the request for and associated verification of supplier related CAPEX throughout NPI

• Conduct value-stream mapping to optimize supply network lead time and flexibility

• Complete the BOM risk assessment and develop plan per part analysis

• Follow through completion of component qualifications by relevant stakeholders, ahead of production need dates

• Reduce complexity of supply chain through commonality optimization & component/supplier rationalization

• Lead all cost engineering activities to converge the bottoms-up cost curve to product cost, maximizing the total cost of ownership (TCO) across the product lifecycle

• Manage ad-hoc cost issues e.g., tariffs / import export cost, and cost inflation

• Drive the design and implementation of new supply chain processes and systems, ensuring they meet business requirements and are built for scale

• Manage project schedules, identify critical path activities, and proactively identify and mitigate risks to keep initiatives on track

• Hold project teams and stakeholders accountable for deliverables and deadlines, navigating organizational complexity to clear roadblocks and drive decisions

• Establish program structure, milestones, and operating rhythms to ensure accountability and drive results across the business

• Drive alignment across stakeholders and influence without formal authority in ambiguous, high-stakes situations

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

• Must be pursuing a bachelor’s or master’s degree in Engineering, or a related technical field.

• Must be returning to school at the end of the internship to continue academic studies for at least one quarter or semester.

• Must be a U.S. Person due to required access to U.S. export-controlled information or facilities; U.S. clearance eligibility may be required depending on program.

• Ability to complete a 12-week in-person internship in one of our offices in summer 2027.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

• Background within:

• Design & development of mechanical and/or electronics devices

• Advanced sourcing activities, including positions working as a commodity/sourcing manager

• Supplier development (technology, process, supply chain, etc.)

• Early supplier engagement, ahead of product/engineering requirement realization

• Exposure to value/procurement engineering or TCO-related work at the component & product level

• Familiarity with developing high-tech products in a high-mix, low-volume environment

US Hourly Range

$32—$45 USD

The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril's total compensation package. Additionally, Anduril offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including:

Benefits

At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you’re supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next. For more information, Explore Our Benefits.

Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams

Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information.

To ensure your safety and help you navigate your job search with confidence, please keep the following critical points in mind:

• No Financial Requests: Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates.

• Please always verify communications: Direct from Anduril: If you receive an email from one of our recruiters, it will only come from an @anduril.com address. Via Agency Partner: If contacted by a recruiting agency for an Anduril role, their email will clearly identify their agency. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency's authenticity by reaching out to contact@anduril.com.

• Exercise Caution with Unsolicited Outreach: If you receive any communication that appears suspicious, contains grammatical errors, or makes unusual requests, do not engage. Always confirm the sender's email domain is @anduril.com before providing any personal information or clicking on links.

• What to Do If You Suspect Fraud: Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to contact@anduril.com. Your proactive caution is invaluable in protecting your personal information and upholding the security and trustworthiness of our recruitment efforts.

Data Privacy

To view Anduril's candidate data privacy policy, please visit https://anduril.com/applicant-privacy-notice/.

By submitting your application, you consent to Anduril Industries using a third-party service provider to conduct pre-employment risk, integrity, and due diligence screening and assessing potential risks as part of your application process. jobs.title: Medical Coding Manager
jobs.description:
About Sprinter Health

 

At Sprinter Health, our mission is reimagining how people access care by bringing it directly into their homes. Nearly 30% of patients in the U.S. skip preventive or chronic care simply because they can’t get to a doctor’s office. For many, the ER becomes their first touchpoint with the healthcare system—driving over $300B in avoidable costs every year.

 

By using the same technologies that power leading marketplace and last-mile platforms, we deliver care where people are, especially those who need it most. So far, we’ve supported more than 2 million patients across 22 states, completed over 130,000 in-home visits, and maintained a 92 NPS. Our team of clinicians, technologists, and operators have raised over $125M to date from investors like a16z, General Catalyst, GV, and Accel.

 

About the Role

 

As the Coding Manager, you will lead Sprinter Health’s Coding team, overseeing medical coders and coding auditors responsible for accurate, compliant, and timely code assignment across our in-home and virtual services. You will own coding operations, quality, and audit programs, and partner closely with clinical, operations, product, and revenue cycle stakeholders.

 

You’ll play a critical role in building a high-performing, learning-oriented coding function that supports clean claims, risk adjustment, quality reporting, and our broader mission to expand access to preventive and chronic care.



What You Will Do

 - Lead, coach, and support a remote team of medical coders (and coding auditors), setting clear expectations, running regular 1:1s, and fostering a culture of trust and respect—not micromanagement.

 - Manage day-to-day coding operations, including work queue oversight, workload balancing, and turnaround time performance, while tracking and reporting on accuracy, productivity, and compliance metrics.

 - Serve as the primary escalation point for coding questions and complex scenarios, partnering with Revenue Cycle, Compliance, and audit resources to understand issues, audit findings, and denial trends.

 - Ensure coding is accurate, complete, and compliant with ICD-10-CM, CPT, HCPCS, CMS, and payer-specific guidelines through strong training, clear policies, and daily oversight.

 - Develop, maintain, and socialize coding policies, playbooks, and job aids that enable consistent, high-quality coding decisions.

 - Design and own a comprehensive coding education program, including new-hire onboarding, ramp plans, role-specific competency checklists, and structured 30/60/90-day milestones.

 - Develop and deliver ongoing training (huddles, workshops, office hours, and written guidance) on guideline updates, payer changes, common error patterns, and Sprinter-specific workflows (e.g., Care+ visits, diagnostics).

 - Create and maintain a centralized, easy-to-use library of training materials—guides, FAQs, tip sheets, and short videos—that coders can rely on in real time.

 - Provide individual coaching based on performance data, audit/denial trends, and observed needs, while supporting coders in maintaining and advancing their professional certifications and continuing education.

 - Foster a strong learning culture by normalizing questions, encouraging peer-to-peer knowledge sharing, recognizing improvements, and reinforcing confidentiality and HIPAA/compliance standards.



You’ll Love this Job If: 

 - You’re energized by developing people, building structured training, and seeing coders grow in confidence and skill.

 - You care deeply about accuracy, integrity, and compliance, and you believe education and clear processes are the best levers to achieve them.

 - You prefer to lead through clarity and collaboration, not micromanagement—you don’t like surprises and value proactive communication.

 - You enjoy turning complex rules into simple, usable guidance for coders and clinicians.

 - You thrive in a tech-forward, high-growth environment where your work directly shapes the future of how coding operates.

 - You’re curious, proactive, and comfortable using data and feedback to refine training, workflows, and team practices.

 - You want to help make Sprinter an employer of choice for coding professionals, where coders feel supported, heard, and proud of their impact.



What We’re Looking For

 - Certification: Active AAPC (e.g., CPC, COC) or AHIMA (CCS-P, CCS) certification.

 - Minimum 5 years of professional coding experience, with at least 2 years in a senior, lead, or supervisory role supporting other coders.

 - Strong understanding of pro-fee coding, including preventive care, primary care, diagnostics, and virtual/telehealth services.

 - Deep knowledge of ICD-10-CM, CPT, HCPCS, modifiers, and national/payer-specific guidelines.

 - Demonstrated experience designing and delivering coding education (e.g., leading trainings/huddles, building guides, mentoring coders).

 - Familiarity with HCC / risk adjustment coding and how coding supports value-based care and quality programs.

 - Experience presenting to and working with external clients or partners, including developing and explaining client-facing reports, analytics, and coding-related insights.

 - Proficiency with EHR systems, encoder/coding software, and productivity/quality reporting tools; experience with Elation and Google Workspace is a plus.

 - Excellent communication and coaching skills, with the ability to explain complex coding topics to both coding and non-coding audiences (internal and external).Proven ability to work independently, prioritize effectively, and manage a remote team.



Technologies We Use

 - EMR: Elation Google Suite (docs, slides, sheets)



 Benefits

 - $80,000 - $110,000 base salary + equity 100% paid health, dental, vision premiums (for families too)

 - Generous parental leave (4 months for birthing parent, 2 months for partners)

 - 401(k) with company match

 - Unlimited PTO + flexible schedule

jobs.title: Lead Physician Assistant (PA)  - Urgent Care
jobs.description:
At ConvenientMD, we’re on a mission to make good health more convenient for all – working to improve how patients and providers experience healthcare in New England. To support this belief, we’re building a team of dedicated professionals who genuinely care about improving lives, are passionate about work that can make a difference, and are driven to learn from one another.

The Opportunity

We’re seeking a compassionate and experienced Physician Associate/Assistant (PA) to join our team as a Lead Provider, responsible for providing exceptional care and making a real impact on the lives of our patients within our urgent care clinic. Lead Providers at ConvenientMD act as clinical leader for all clinical staff, mentoring and supporting new-grad providers as well as allied healthcare professionals.

This role is perfect for a PA who thrives in a collaborative environment, enjoys mentorship, and is passionate about delivering high-quality care.

Your Impact

• Provide Patient-Centered Care: Conduct health assessments, physical exams, and review medical histories to address short- and long-term patient needs while staying committed to high-quality, efficient patient care. Assess patient health: Interview patients, perform physical examinations, obtain, update, and study medical histories. Determine abnormal conditions: Administer or order diagnostic tests (e.g., x-rays, electrocardiograms, laboratory studies) and interpret test results. Perform therapeutic procedures: Administer injections and immunizations, suture, manage wounds and infections. Educate and counsel: Empower patients with knowledge about their health, describe therapeutic regimens, give information on normal growth and development, discuss family planning, and wellness through counseling and guidance.

• Documentation & Compliance: Prepare clear, complete, accurate, and legible medical records for each patient under your care. Type, edit, and electronically sign all office notes, reports and records using EMR in accordance with company policies. Maintain a safe and clean working environment in compliance with company and state procedures, rules, and regulations. Protect patients and employees by adhering to infection-control policies and protocols. Comply with legal and professional requirements including studying existing and new legislation, anticipating future legislation, enforcing adherence to requirements, advising management on needed actions.

• Collaborate with a Team: Work collaboratively and pro-actively with other providers and health care practitioners within your clinic to efficiently treat patients, and plan coordinated, efficient, and thoughtful dispositions (including transfer), all in a timely manner.

• Continuing Education & Mentorship: Act as a clinic leader, especially when the Practice Manager is not in-clinic. Provide support and mentorship to new-graduate providers as well as other clinic staff. Maintain professional and technical knowledge by attending educational workshops, reviewing professional publications, establishing personal networks, and participating in professional societies. Act as a preceptor to new provider staff, providing information, educational opportunities, and experiential growth opportunities.

Who You Are

• Education, Licensure, & Certifications: Master's degree and certification by Physician Assistant (PA) certifying body. Must have and maintain a DEA license with no restrictions. Basic Life Support (BLS) certification: American Heart Association or American Red Cross BLS certification. We do not accept CPR, ACLS certifications, or online only classes.

• Relevant experience: Clinical experience in emergency medicine, urgent care, or ambulatory care setting is preferred.

• Strong leadership skills: Willing and able to mentor provider as well as non-provider clinic staff.

• Excellent team player: Enjoy collaborating with others and being a part of a strong team dynamic.

• Proactive and confident communicator (written and verbal): Foreshadows and elevates concerns as they arise, unafraid of professional directness both with colleagues and patients.

• Compassionate, authentic, and patient focused: Supports patients through kindness; demonstrating understanding for others and contributing to the creating a community of belonging.

• Technically savvy: Proficient with Microsoft Office Suite or related software and clinical management systems (EMR).

• Strong knowledge of: Principles and processes for providing customer and personal services, including customer needs assessment, meeting quality standards for services, and evaluation of customer satisfaction. Applicable federal, state, and local laws and regulations including the requirements of the HIPAA and OSHA and applicable state rules and regulations pertinent to medical practices. Relevant drugs and their chemical composition, structure, and properties of substances and of the chemical processes and transformations that they undergo. Non-pharmaceutical patient care aids, their applicable uses, and relevance to patient care. Current principles, methods, and procedures for the delivery of medical evaluation, diagnosis, and treatment.

#NHPR

Why You'll Love Working With Us

• Collaborative team environment that encourages professional growth

• Urgent care services at no cost to our team members and their families

• Extensive benefit offerings including health, dental, and vision coverage, company paid short-term disability, and optional pet insurance

• 401k match after one year of service

• Access to our primary care (depending on location)

jobs.title: Maintenance Supervisor
jobs.description:
Company Overview: 
 
IRCA is a leading international provider of semi-finished ingredients for the bakery, pastry and gelato markets, serving independent producers as well as large food manufacturers (e.g. CPG). Core products include chocolate, chocolate decorations, creams, pastry mixes, gelato ingredients, and other bakery / pastry ingredients. 
 
The Company, headquartered in Italy, was acquired by Advent International, the global Private Equity firm, in July 2022, and has a strong track record of growth over the last decade. IRCA has made 2 bolt-on acquisitions in the areas of candied fruits (Cesarin) and pistachio ingredients (Anastasi) in 2022, and recently entered exclusive negotiations to acquire a leading manufacturer of sweet and cereal products in Europe and the US. The target’s business focuses on high value add specialty ingredients for the Food Manufacturers segment, with a portfolio that incorporates a range of products including sweet particulates, chocolate confections, baked inclusions, variegates and fruit purées. 
 
This transformative deal would create a global leader in the semi-finished ingredients industry, with 22 manufacturing facilities in Europe, US and Vietnam and a combined €1 billion of revenues (2022). 
 
Job Purpose: 
This key position provides leadership and direction to the facility maintenance department. The successful candidate will be responsible for facility projects and repair, maintenance, and installation of machines, tools, and equipment in manufacturing operations. Responsible for controlling all causes of failure and ensuring full useful equipment life in coordination with daily maintenance completed by operating personnel.

jobs.title: Head of Finance
jobs.description:
WHAT WE DO

Build the insurance behind the physical world.

The world is building data centers, energy projects, hospitals, schools, and critical infrastructure. Every one of those projects needs insurance to move forward. Yet the process of getting that insurance still depends on scattered documents, manual work, and weeks of back-and-forth.

 

Shepherd is rebuilding commercial insurance with software, data, AI, and deep underwriting expertise. We started in construction and energy, where understanding the specifics of a project matters and better decisions have consequences far beyond a screen.

 

We develop insurance products, decide which risks to insure and how to price them, and partner with established insurers to back the coverage. We own the platform our team uses to turn complex submissions into coverage for the builders and operators shaping the world around us.

 

Real problems. Real ownership.

Our engineers, designers, underwriters, and actuaries build together. The problems span turning messy documents into reliable data, making pricing more precise, and designing AI agents that can take on increasingly complex underwriting work.

 

The ambition is a platform where experts spend more time on judgment and relationships, supported by software that handles the work around them. Join us to build systems whose decisions help real projects get built.

 

630+ customers / $500B+ insured project value

 
[https://app.ashbyhq.com/api/images/user-content/cfdfd0b4-accb-41e6-8804-1216b89e5f82/0348cf6f-15dd-401e-8c20-de06e7a553fc/full-team.jpg]
 


OUR INVESTORS

Capital to build. Partners to grow with.

$67M total funding / $42M Series B in March 2026

 

Shepherd is backed by Intact Private Capital, Costanoa Ventures, Spark Capital, Susa Ventures, and Y Combinator. In March 2026, we announced a $42M Series B led by Intact Private Capital, bringing our total funding to $67M.

 

Intact is also a capacity partner. Alongside its investment, Intact works with Shepherd to bring insurance products to market. That relationship connects our platform and underwriting expertise with the resources of a global insurer.

 

A bigger opportunity ahead

We are investing in new insurance products, our underwriting team, and the path toward autonomous underwriting. For the people joining Shepherd, that means the chance to shape both the technology and the business it makes possible.

 

Our backing brings together investors who build technology companies and partners who understand insurance. We are building a company that earns the confidence of both.

 
[https://app.ashbyhq.com/api/images/user-content/cfdfd0b4-accb-41e6-8804-1216b89e5f82/1441bf79-1d14-43aa-be40-ef718b7fdac3/nyc-wide.jpg]
 


WHAT WE DO

Commercial insurance still runs on processes built decades ago. Underwriting is slow, and pricing leans on broad averages instead of the specifics of each risk. Technology can change how commercial risk is priced and managed, as long as it's paired with real underwriting expertise. The companies that get this right will shape the next era of the industry, and Shepherd intends to lead it.

Shepherd is a Managing General Underwriter (MGU) building the fastest and smartest AI-native commercial risk platform in the industry, where underwriters, data, and automation work together. The result is faster decisions for our broker partners and pricing that reflects the actual risk we’re covering.

We started where the gap is widest: construction and energy, two of the most complex and highest-hazard segments in commercial insurance. In 2027 we will expand our platform to more industries and more products, reaching wider into commercial insurance with a plan of $1B+ in premiums by the end of 2028. Our mission is to make risk frictionless for the builders and operators shaping the physical world, from concept through construction and into decades of operation.


🚀 OUR INVESTORS

Shepherd has raised over $67M, including a $42M Series B led by Intact Private Capital. Intact also partners with Shepherd to provide capacity across its insurance products. Shepherd is also backed by leading institutional investors, including Costanoa Ventures, Spark Capital, Susa Ventures, and Y Combinator.


🤝 OUR TEAM

We're a team of technologists and insurance enthusiasts, bridging the two worlds together. Check out our About https://www.shepherdinsurance.com/about page to learn more.


HEAD OF FINANCE


ABOUT YOU

You are a finance leader who wants to build the financial engine of a fast-growing insurance company. You’ve owned the plan, the numbers, and the controls, and you understand how capital and capacity shape an insurance business. You want to do the best work of your career at a company where finance sits at the center of how we grow.

You’d be a great fit if you have:

 - 10+ years in finance, spanning FP&A, accounting, and strategic finance, including 4+ years leading teams at a venture-backed or high-growth company.

 - Insurance finance experience at an MGA/MGU, carrier, reinsurer, or insurtech. You know commission and fee revenue, premium and claims flows, fiduciary accounts, bordereaux, and carrier and reinsurance reporting.

 - Familiarity with risk-bearing structures such as captives, sidecars, quota shares, and fronting arrangements, and the accounting, cash, collateral, and regulatory requirements that come with them.

 - A track record of running annual planning, forecasting, and budget-versus-actuals reviews on integrated models across revenue, headcount, OpEx, and cash.

 - Strong command of close, audit, tax, treasury, and internal controls, including managing outsourced accounting partners.

 - Experience leading or partnering closely with revenue operations, business operations, and analytics teams.

 - Executive presence with a board, investors, carriers, and reinsurers. Fundraising experience is a plus.

 - A bias toward systems and automation, including building finance and payments infrastructure with engineering.

 - A bachelor’s degree in finance, accounting, economics, or a related field. CPA, CFA, or MBA is a plus.


ABOUT THE ROLE

As Head of Finance, you will own Shepherd’s financial planning, accounting, controls, and reporting, and lead the operations teams that run our go-to-market engine. You’ll manage our Finance Lead and the Revenue Operations, Business Operations, and Analytics teams, work closely with the CEO, and partner with our Reinsurance and Capital Strategy leader as we add risk-bearing capacity.

In this role, you will:

Finance and planning

 - Own the annual operating plan, long-range model, and monthly forecast and budget-versus-actuals reviews across revenue, headcount, OpEx, and cash.

 - Build product-level contribution margin views so each new launch is judged on its economics.

 - Own reporting packages for the board, investors, carriers, and reinsurers, and support future fundraising.

Capital, accounting, and controls

 - Partner with both our Chief Insurance Officer and Reinsurance and Capital Strategy leader on the finance side of new risk-bearing structures, including captives, sidecars, quota shares, and fronting arrangements: modeling, accounting treatment, capital and collateral needs, and reporting.

 - Build the entity, treasury, and cash infrastructure those structures need, including premium trust and fiduciary accounts, collateral, intercompany flows, and regulatory filings.

 - Build scalable carrier payment tracking and bordereaux reconciliation across our carrier partners.

 - Oversee close, audit, tax, and spend controls, and manage our outsourced accounting partner.

Operations

 - Lead Analytics, Revenue Operations, and Business Operations across submission attribution, broker tiering, quota setting and compensation, underwriter enablement, partnerships, and marketing infrastructure.

 - Tie plan, pipeline, and performance data together in one operating cadence.

 - Hire, coach, and grow the finance and operations teams.

This is a position based in our New York City or San Francisco offices


COMPENSATION

The base salary range for this role is $275,000 – $400,000, plus an annual performance bonus and equity in Shepherd. Offers within the range depend on location and experience.


HOW WE WORK

Shepherd runs on four values. Here's what each one means in this seat.

 - 🚀 Think big, build big. We exist to protect progress and the industries that rely on it. You’re building the finance function for a company planning to reach $1B+ in premium, so the models, controls, and entity structures get designed for that scale from the start.

 - 🤝 Win together. We rise as one. We support each other, raise the bar, and celebrate collective success. As our first Head of Finance, you set the standard for how every team plans, spends, and measures results.

 - 🔄 Cross the aisle. Collaboration wins. We listen deeply, work across boundaries, and prioritize shared success over individual lanes. Underwriting, reinsurance and capital, engineering, and leadership all rely on finance to make decisions, and much of this job is making those partnerships work.

 - 🔥 Go get it. We act with urgency, move with confidence, take smart risks, and push forward with intention. The plan, the controls, and the structures behind our next stage of growth are still to be built. You build them and make the calls.


🌟 BENEFITS

🏥 Premium Healthcare
100% contribution to top-tier health, dental, and vision

👶 Fertility Benefits & Family Building Support

🌴 Unlimited PTO
Flexibility to take the time off, recharge, and perform

🍽️ Daily Lunches, Dinners & Snacks
We work together, and enjoy meals together too

🏢 SF, NYC, Dallas–Fort Worth, Chicago & LA Offices

📈 Professional Development
Access to premium coaching, including leadership development

💵 Competitive 401(k) Plan

🐶 Dog-Friendly Office
Plenty of dogs to play with and make friends with in the SF office


HOW WE WORK

Shepherd runs on four values. Here's what each one means in this seat.

 - Think big, build big. We exist to protect progress and the industries that rely on it. The work here is aimed at a system that runs on its own, and the roadmap gets sequenced backward from that rather than forward from what's easy.

 - Win together. We rise as one. We support each other, raise the bar, and celebrate collective success. Come set a standard the rest of the team inherits.

The best product calls here come from engineers who've sat with underwriters and underwriters who understand where the model breaks, and much of this job is listening closely enough on both sides to make that happen.

 - Go get it. We act with urgency, move with confidence, take smart risks, and push forward with intention. Nobody hands you the roadmap, the data, or the meeting invite. You pull the failing runs, book the time with the underwriters, and decide what matters.

jobs.title: Enterprise Workday Administration
jobs.description:
As our Enterprise Workday Administrator, you will be the driving force behind the success of our Workday platform. You’ll take full ownership of Workday, partnering closely with our implementation vendor, HR, Finance, and IS leadership to ensure a seamless launch and ongoing operational excellence. This is a highly visible, strategic role where your work will directly shape the way the organization leverages Workday for years to come.

WHAT YOU'LL DO:

Workday Ownership & Configuration

• Manage Workday tenant configuration, business processes, and system settings.
• Lead updates, releases, and system enhancements.
• Maintain documentation, configuration guides, and training materials.
• Evaluate and implement new Workday features to maximize organizational impact.

Troubleshooting & Tier 3 Support

• Serve as technical escalation point for complex Workday issues.
• Train and enable Tier 1 & Tier 2 support teams to resolve issues effectively.
• Manage ticket queues and resolve challenging system problems.

Change Management & Cross-Functional Leadership

• Lead Workday change control committee with HR, Finance, and IS stakeholders.
• Facilitate decisions for system changes and enhancements.
• Communicate updates, secure approvals, and implement changes, with organizational impact.
• Promote adoption and effective communication of Workday changes.
• Manage vendor relationships and third-party support to optimize system performance.

MUST HAVE:

• Education: Bachelor’s in Information Systems, Information Technologies, Information Technology, Computer Science, or a closely related field with equivalent experience.
• Technical Skills: Proficient in troubleshooting, tier-3 support, report building, and system documentation.
• Workday Experience: 7+ years of hands-on Workday administration, including tenant management, business processes, security roles and access control, integrations (EIB, Core Connect, APIs, Workday Studio), reporting, and release management.
• Technical Proficiency: Experience with cloud platforms, enterprise integrations, Microsoft Office 365, and data reporting/analytics tools (Prism, calculated fields, dashboards).
• Professional Development: Willingness to pursue Workday certifications (training provided) and stay current on best practices.
• Work Authorization Requirement: Candidates must be legally authorized to work in the United States on a permanent basis. This position does not offer visa sponsorship now or in the future.

NICE TO HAVE:

• Enterprise Systems & Platforms: Experience managing integrations with third-party systems, Workday security management, identity and access management systems, and understanding of IT security best practices.
• Professional Certifications: Workday certifications (HCM, Finance, Security), additional Workday security or reporting certifications. CompTIA A+ Certification, or other IT certifications.
• Experience: Application administration, integrations/interface management, leading committees, supporting system implementations.

ADDITIONAL SKILLS CRITICAL FOR SUCCESS:

• Strategic Thinking & Process Improvement: Analyze processes and data to identify improvements, optimize workflows, and guide system design for long-term effectiveness.
• Technical & Analytical Expertise: Expert in system administration, process management, integrations, and reporting. Strong troubleshooting and problem-solving skills with knowledge of cybersecurity, data privacy, disaster recovery, and compliance. Able to support complex, multi-unit environments efficiently.
• Leadership & Change Management: Lead change committees, influence stakeholders, mentor support teams, and guide system updates, implementations, and enhancements with clear communication and organizational buy-in.
• Project Management & Execution: Plan and manage system upgrades and go-lives, juggling multiple priorities and deadlines while maintaining accurate documentation and high attention to detail.
• Communication & Interpersonal Skills: Translate technical concepts for non-technical users, present to internal audiences, and build strong relationships across HR, Finance, and IT.
• Adaptability & Learning Agility: Adjust quickly to system updates, process changes, and evolving organizational needs while embracing continuous learning and innovation.
• Customer Service & Team Orientation: Foster a collaborative, solutions-focused mindset and prioritize user satisfaction alongside organizational goals.

WHY YOU’LL LOVE THIS ROLE:

Take the lead in shaping our Workday platform and make a real impact! In this highly visible, strategic role, you’ll guide a smooth go-live, influence system design, and collaborate closely with HR, Finance, and IT leaders to drive meaningful organizational change. You’ll implement lasting improvements, support over 2,000 users across multiple business units, and manage integrations, reporting, and system security at scale. Grow as a recognized Workday expert while thriving within a supportive, solutions-focused team that values innovation, continuous learning, and professional growth.

jobs.title: Business Process Governance Specialist
jobs.description:
Western Digital's Global Supply Chain Organization (GSCO) is building a Business Process Governance (BPG) program — a new, centralized governance function responsible for the integrity, currency, and audit-readiness of all business processes and procedures across the full GSCO. This program replaces fragmented, function-by-function documentation practices with a single, durable governance model that keeps policy and operational practice in sync, satisfies Internal and External Audit control requirements, and creates a standing mechanism for continuous improvement and digitalization.

The Business Process Governance Specialist is a core member of the BPG team, working directly under the BPG Program Lead. This role is responsible for executing the operational backbone of the program — procedure lifecycle management, audit control mapping, adherence assessment, governance tooling operations, training coordination, and continuous improvement tracking — across six GSCO functions and an active library of approximately 72 governed procedures.

This is not a content authorship role. Procedure content is owned and written by functional SMEs. The BPG Specialist is the governance engine: ensuring every procedure has a named owner, is mapped to its audit controls, is reviewed on schedule, and reflects operational reality.

Note: One of the three BPG Specialist hires will be designated as the Governance Technology & Operations lead based on candidate profile and experience, with additional responsibility for tooling selection support, IT project coordination, and platform administration.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

Procedure Lifecycle Management

• Inventory, assess, and classify all GSCO procedures across assigned functions using established BPG framework standards
• Assign and confirm named procedure ownership in coordination with Functional VPs and their designated POCs
• Manage the full procedure lifecycle: intake, review scheduling, version control, approval routing, publication, and archival
• Identify and document procedure gaps; hand off gap remediation packages to functional owners with templates, standards, and deadlines
• Escalate missed review deadlines per the BPG escalation framework
• Apply the governance model to the procedure library across all assigned functions

Audit Control Mapping & Readiness Support

• Map all assigned procedures to applicable audit controls (Internal Audit, BCMS, IMS) using the BPG control mapping standard
• Maintain the procedure-to-control mapping registry; keep it current through procedure reviews and audit activity
• Support pre-audit readiness reviews with Functional Owners; surface documentation gaps before audit windows open
• Maintain audit intake log; route audit evidence requests to the appropriate Functional Owner with SLA clock initiated
• Track SLA compliance by Functional Owner; escalate misses per program framework
• Capture lessons learned post-audit; contribute findings to framework refinement.

Governance Tooling Operations

• Operate the BPG governance platform as the day-to-day system administrator: document repository, approval workflow, version control, audit trail, and automated review reminders
• Configure tooling for each function
• Ensure access controls are maintained in alignment with the ownership model
• Identify and escalate tooling gaps or workflow failures

For the Governance Technology & Operations designated hire — additional responsibilities:

• Lead the governance tooling evaluation and selection process in partnership with IT
• Define and document BPG tooling functional requirements for IT engagement
• Project-manage the tooling implementation from selection through go-live
• Serve as the primary BPG liaison to IT for platform configuration, enhancements, and issue resolution
• Own platform administration ongoing post-implementation

Review Cadence & Training Coordination

• Set, schedule, and track procedure review cadences weighted by risk across assigned functions
• Trigger training cycles tied to procedure review schedules; assign training to named owners and super-users
• Track training completion rates; escalate overdue completions per program framework
• Report training status to functional leads and BPG Program Lead

Continuous Improvement

• Surface efficiency, automation, and digitalization opportunities identified through procedure review and adherence assessment activity
• Synthesize and document CI opportunities; route to appropriate functional leaders via BPG Program Lead
• Track CI opportunities through to resolution; maintain CI KPI inputs (volume and resolution rate)
• Collaborate with Functional Owners to define and design procedure and process improvements where assigned

Pilot Execution & Rollout Support

• Execute BPG pilot activities in Sourcing P2P (Phase 1) including procedure inventory, gap identification, control mapping, tooling configuration, and training coordination
• Support pilot retrospective; contribute to framework documentation updates
• Extend framework function-by-function as rollout progresses

Required

• 5+ years of experience in process governance, procedure lifecycle management, audit support, compliance program management, or COE/PMO operations
• Demonstrated experience managing a procedure or document library at scale — including ownership assignment, version control, review cadence, and audit trail requirements
• Working knowledge of audit control frameworks; ability to map process documentation to control requirements (Internal Audit, ISO, SOX, or equivalent)
• Exposure to or experience within Supply Chain, Procurement, or Global Operations environments — enough to engage functional SMEs as a credible peer
• Strong project management skills — able to manage multiple workstreams, track deliverables across stakeholders, and escalate systematically
• Experience working in or alongside cross-functional teams; able to build working relationships with Functional VPs, procedure owners, and operational SMEs
• High proficiency with document management platforms, workflow tools, or governance systems
• Clear, structured written communication — able to produce framework documentation, gap analyses, and status reports without heavy supervision

Preferred

• Hands-on experience as an Internal or External Auditor (not only supporting audits) strongly preferred, including testing controls, evaluating evidence, and documenting findings.
• Familiarity with AI-enabled training tools or process education platforms
• Experience coordinating with IT on digital transformation projects.
• Background in continuous improvement methodologies (Lean, Six Sigma, or equivalent)

Why This Role

This program has direct executive sponsorship, a defined pilot-and-extend roadmap, and a mandate to close a recurring audit finding across a global supply chain organization. The BPG Specialist joins at program launch — shaping how governance operates, not inheriting someone else's framework. The work is visible, the scope is real, and the path from pilot to full GSCO coverage is already chartered.

jobs.title: Trade Compliance Manager/Senior Manager
jobs.location: Denver, CO, Santa Fe, NM, or New York, NY
jobs.description:
At Maybell Quantum, we're redefining the future of computing. As a venture-backed quantum hardware innovator experiencing rapid growth, we build the cryogenic infrastructure that quantum computers run on — dilution refrigerators, cryogenic RF wiring, and the related systems used by quantum computing companies, national labs, and research institutions worldwide. Quantum computers will be as transformative to the next 30 years as the internet was to the last 30—and our team is creating the hardware foundation to make this revolution possible.

Position Overview

We're seeking a Trade Compliance Manager/Senior Manager to own trade compliance for Maybell globally. This is the first dedicated compliance hire at the company; the function currently runs through the President with outside counsel support. You will build it.

Compliance at Maybell is not a back-office function. Our products sit squarely inside the emerging export control regime for quantum technology, and getting it right determines what we can ship, to whom, and how our engineering teams across four countries are able to work together. We operate from Denver, with facilities in Münster, Germany and Helsinki, Finland, are establishing operations in Singapore, and ship to customers across North America, Europe, and Asia.

The work is substantive from day one. We have active shipments requiring licensing, a distributor relationship in Korea with end-user obligations, engineering collaboration across US, German, Finnish, and Singapore teams that raises deemed export questions, and a product line whose classification sits in a part of the Commerce Control List that is still developing.

This is not a documentation or logistics coordination role. You are the decision-maker on classification and licensing, and you will be expected to defend those decisions. The role does not report into Operations, Engineering, or Sales, by design, and the compliance answer is not negotiated after the commercial commitment is made — you will be in the room early. You'll partner closely with Operations, Engineering, Sales, Supply Chain, IT, and HR, and report to the President.

Key Responsibilities

Classification and Licensing

• Classify Maybell products, components, software, and technical data under the EAR, including the quantum-specific ECCNs (3A90x, 4A9xx series) and related controls

• Determine license requirements per transaction; prepare, file, and manage BIS license applications and license exception determinations

• Obtain and actively manage the export licenses required to establish Maybell's Singapore operations, and keep them in good standing as those operations run

• Manage equivalent processes with BAFA in Germany, Singapore Customs, the Finnish Ministry for Foreign Affairs, and other national regimes as our footprint requires

• Maintain classification records and jurisdictional determinations to an auditable standard

Deemed Exports and Technical Data

• Own the deemed export program: assess nationality-based access requirements for controlled technical data across our Denver, Münster, Helsinki, and Singapore engineering teams

• Partner with IT and engineering leadership to define access controls on CAD, PLM, and technical documentation systems — you decide who may have access; IT implements it

• Support hiring and onboarding decisions where foreign national access to controlled technology is implicated

• Maintain a current log of employee nationality and immigration status as required under the EAR and applicable local regulations

Transaction Screening and Diligence

• Run restricted and denied party screening across customers, distributors, suppliers, and visitors

• Conduct end-use and end-user diligence, including red flag escalation

• Identify and apply for any licenses a specific deal requires, and track them through approval before commitments are made

• Support commercial negotiations on export-related contract terms — license conditions, end-user certifications, re-export obligations, and distributor undertakings

Supply Chain and Partner Compliance

• Work closely with the Supply Chain team to ensure Maybell's suppliers and partners, such as regional distributors, comply with the EAR, including export compliance diligence at onboarding and appropriate contractual commitments

• Review supply chain strategy for export control implications, including sourcing locations, supplier jurisdictions, and where controlled technical data must be shared

• Confirm that outsourced parts, and the technical data provided to suppliers to build them, are properly classified and authorized before release

• Monitor emerging supply chain risks such as new controls, entity listings, and sanctions changes affecting suppliers and partners, and drive mitigation such as alternate sourcing or additional licensing as necessary

Travel and Ongoing Monitoring

• Develop and maintain the staff travel policy to ensure business travel, including devices and technical data carried abroad, complies with export control requirements

• Actively monitor employee travel declarations, IT reports, and other ongoing compliance activities to ensure Maybell remains compliant with applicable export control regimes

Program and Governance

• Build and maintain Maybell's Export Compliance Program: written procedures, training, recordkeeping, internal audit, and escalation paths

• Deliver role-specific training to departments

• Manage outside trade counsel and consultants; scope their work and own the internal decisions

• Prepare compliance materials for investor and customer diligence

Authority and Escalation

• Exercise explicit authority to hold a shipment, transfer, or technical data disclosure pending compliance resolution — that authority is not advisory and does not require sign-off from Operations or Sales

• Escalate unresolved conflicts between a compliance determination and a commercial or operational commitment to the CEO, not through the functions with delivery or revenue accountability

Qualifications

• 5+ years in export controls or trade compliance for Manager, or 8+ years with multi-jurisdictional program ownership for Senior Manager, in each case with direct hands-on responsibility for classification and licensing under the EAR

• Demonstrated experience filing and managing BIS licenses, not just supporting someone who does

• Working knowledge of deemed export requirements and how to operate a program in a multinational engineering organization

• Experience in hardware manufacturing with genuinely controlled products — aerospace, defense, semiconductor capital equipment, scientific instrumentation, or similar

• Judgment and spine; this role exists to say no when no is the right answer, sometimes to founders, sometimes at quarter end

• Exposure to EU dual-use regulation and at least one national European regime (German BAFA, Finnish Ministry for Foreign Affairs, Dutch national controls) preferred

• Experience building a compliance program rather than inheriting one preferred

• Familiarity with emerging technology controls — quantum, advanced computing, semiconductors — preferred

• Experience supporting distributor and reseller channels with end-user obligations preferred

• A law degree is not required — this is not a legal role

What We Offer

• Competitive Compensation: Base salary range $130,000–$180,000, plus meaningful equity participation and annual bonus eligibility. Final title (Manager or Senior Manager) and base salary will be determined based on depth of licensing experience and multi-jurisdictional exposure.

• Real Authority: You hold and exercise the authority to stop a shipment, transfer, or disclosure pending compliance resolution, and escalation runs to the CEO.

• Growth Trajectory: A direct path to building and leading Maybell's global trade compliance function from the ground up.

• Impact: Direct responsibility for how one of the most consequential technologies of our era moves across borders.

• Exceptional Team: Collaboration with world-class scientists, engineers, and operators.

• Comprehensive Benefits: Medical, dental, and vision insurance, 401(k), and paid time off.

At Maybell Quantum, we're solving incredibly challenging problems at the cutting edge of physics and engineering. If you're excited about owning the decisions that determine where one of the most transformative technologies of our lifetime can go, we want to hear from you.

Maybell is an equal opportunity employer. Because this role involves access to export-controlled technology, we may be required to verify your status as a U.S. person or to obtain export authorization; we assess this consistently with applicable law and do not discriminate on the basis of citizenship or national origin beyond what U.S. export regulations require.

jobs.title: Head of Strategic Accounts
jobs.description:
About 9fin

9fin is the AI platform powering global debt markets — the world’s largest asset class at over $145 trillion.

Debt markets are vast, global, and mission-critical, yet still run on fragmented data, PDFs, and manual workflows. 9fin replaces this broken infrastructure with a single platform that centralises proprietary credit data, deep analysis, and high-value workflows across global markets.

Today, 9fin powers teams at 300+ blue-chip institutions worldwide, including global banks, asset managers, private equity firms, law firms, and advisors. The business is scaling at exceptional speed, with rapid expansion in the US and best-in-class retention driven by deep workflow adoption.

We’re at a defining inflection point. With proven product-market fit and strong, global market pull, 9fin is accelerating toward becoming the category-defining platform for debt markets worldwide.




ABOUT THE ROLE

 

We’re looking for a Head of Strategic Accounts, US to lead the top tier of our commercial organization — the largest, most complex accounts driving 9fin’s next phase of growth. Strategics is our top segment: a targeted book of our largest ARR accounts across the global banks, top-tier law firms, multi-strategy hedge funds, asset managers, and private equity firms who set the standard for how credit intelligence is bought and used.

 

You’ll build and lead a team of ~5–6 senior relationship managers in New York, each owning a small portfolio of strategic accounts in a hybrid Account Management and Enterprise Sales role. You’ll partner closely with our Head of Strategic Accounts, EMEA to run a globally coordinated segment and work with senior Customer Success partners at the account level.

This is a builder role for a leader who has personally carried a large number, sold enterprise-scale deals into financial services, and knows how to raise the bar on rigor, presence, and multi-year deal execution.

This role requires 3 days in our NYC office.




WHAT YOU’LL WORK ON

Every day is different, but here’s an example of the kind of things you’ll work on:

 

 - Lead the US Strategics team to consistent, forecastable delivery quarter over quarter across a book of $5M+ ARR accounts.

 - Coach and manage a team of ~5–6 Strategic Account Managers covering our most important banks, asset managers, hedge funds, private equity firms, and law firms in the US.

 - Drive multi-year deal execution, lock in early renewals, and structure enterprise agreements that grow durably over time.

 - Coach the team through complex commercial motions — MSAs, procurement, legal review, and executive alignment at the MD, Partner, PM, Head of Desk, and C-suite level.

 - Run weekly segment reviews focused on deals moved, deals at risk, pipeline health, and account-level path-to-close plans.

 - Set the operating cadence for the segment. Enforce our 3-day office minimum, and drive territory planning, account mapping, and a shared deal methodology across the team.

 - Partner with the EMEA Head of Strategic Accounts to build geographic reciprocity, with US AMs backing up EMEA coverage on global accounts, and vice versa.

 - Work in a “two-in-the-box” model with senior CSMs (product and usage) and Sales Engineering (pre-sales), and partner across Enablement, Rev Ops, Marketing, and Product to remove barriers to growth.

 - Be the senior voice of our strategic clients into Product and Engineering — translating segment-level themes across credit, leveraged finance, restructuring, distressed, and private credit into a clear point of view on the roadmap.

 - Represent 9fin externally with the C-suite — at client offsites, executive briefings, industry conferences, and roundtables — and become a recognised name in US debt markets.

 - Build the operating system for the Strategics segment — deal reviews, path-to-close proposals, territory planning, and account planning frameworks that scale.




ABOUT YOU

This role will be a great fit if you:

 

 - Have 12+ years of enterprise B2B sales experience, including 4+ years leading strategic or enterprise sales teams selling into financial services (banks, asset managers, hedge funds, PE firms), law firms, or a mix.

 - Have personally carried and consistently exceeded a large individual quota on multi-million-dollar strategic accounts, and can point to specific accounts you’ve grown from $X to $Y and explain exactly how.

 - Bring a consultative approach to selling and want to become a strategic partner to our clients

 - Have deep familiarity with capital markets, credit, or the debt markets ecosystem across credit, leveraged finance, restructuring, distressed, and private credit — you can hold your own with a restructuring lawyer, a leveraged finance banker, or a credit PM.

 - Have led teams through multi-year deal execution and understand what it takes to secure meaningful year-over-year uplifts, early renewals, and complex enterprise agreements.

 - Can coach reps through complex procurement, MSA negotiation, legal review, and executive alignment at the MD, Partner, PM, Head of Desk, and C-suite level.

 - Bring C-suite presence and cross-organizational credibility. You show up sharp, prepared, and trusted by both your team and your customers.

 - Are a proactive coach, not a reactive manager. You share process, mentor your reps, and help them plan deals in advance rather than reacting to slipped forecasts.

 - Have run a disciplined operating cadence — weekly deal reviews, forecast rigor, territory and account planning, and a shared deal methodology across the team.

 - Are commercially sharp and operationally rigorous, and can be a credible senior voice of your team’s clients into Product and Engineering.

 - Build trust across a matrixed commercial organization and can partner effectively with Customer Success, Sales Engineering, Enablement, Rev Ops, Marketing, and Product.

 - Set a high bar and lead through presence and standards rather than fear. You drive accountability without burning your team out.

 - Thrive in ambitious, fast-moving environments where expectations are high, opportunities are abundant, and no two days look the same.




OUR BENEFITS

We’re a scaling start up and we enjoy sharing our success, when the company succeeds, we always reinvest that in our people. We also offer huge amounts of responsibility, an abundance of opportunity for growth and a platform to truly excel.

Financial & Insurance

 - Competitive Salary: $180,000-$215,000  

 - Commission & Equity

 - 401(k) (9fin pay 3%, employee contributions are uncapped)

 - Private Health Insurance, with Dental and Vision

 - Paid sick leave

 - Disability Insurance (New York)

Time off

 - 25 vacation days per year

 - Local public holiday

 - Work abroad for up to 3 months a year

 - 1 month paid sabbatical after 5 years of service

 - Enhanced parental leave & flexible working arrangements available

Training & Culture

 - Professional learning and development budget

 - Bi-annual team socials

 - Summer and Winter company social events

Hybrid Policy

9fin is a hybrid company, and the office is a regular part of how we work. From January 2027, all employees will work from their designated 9fin office on Tuesdays and Wednesdays. Some teams may be asked to be in the office more often, where the nature of their work calls for it. For the rest of the week, you may work from wherever works best for you and your team. Your Talent Partner will share hybrid working details for this role.



9fin is an equal opportunities employer 

At 9fin we are dedicated to building and promoting a fair and inclusive workplace where everyone can reach their full potential and truly belong. We recognize that building diverse teams enables a more creative and productive environment. If you’re excited about this role but your experience doesn’t perfectly align with the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. You might just be who we’re looking for — either for this role, or perhaps another.
